articles.title_orig: Police officer fatally shot while responding to call in West Philadelphia
articles.title_zh: Police officer fatally shot while responding to call in West Philadelphia
articles.content_orig:
10-year police veteran Shane Seiber was killed after responding to a report of a man with a gun
A Philadelphia police officer was fatally shot and another was wounded on Saturday after responding to a report of a man with a gun, authorities said.
Shane Seiber, 40, was killed early on Saturday morning in West Philadelphia , according to the city’s police commissioner, Kevin Bethel.
Seiber, a 10-year veteran of the Philadelphia police department, and the other officer were transported to the Penn Presbyterian medical center, where the surviving officer underwent surgery. He was listed in stable condition, Bethel said.
Bethel also said a suspect was in custody.
Citing law enforcements sources, the Philadelphia Inquirer identified that suspect as Eric Lewis. The Inquirer also reported that Lewis, 35, was employed by Philadelphia’s municipal water department.
Pennsylvania’s governor, Josh Shapiro, said he ordered flags to fly at half-mast for Seiber. He is survived by his wife and two children: a boy, age seven, and a girl, three.
Seiber was at least the 376th Philadelphia police department officer to die in the line of duty since 1851, according to the Officer Down Memorial Page , which honors US law enforcement personnel who died while on the job. He was the 129th of those officers to die from gunfire, the memorial page said.

articles.title_orig: Trump fumes at ‘stain’ on Norway after missing out on Nobel Peace Prize
articles.title_zh: Trump fumes at ‘stain’ on Norway after missing out on Nobel Peace Prize
articles.content_orig:
The US president lashed out after former UN official Navi Pillay was awarded the prize, claiming the decision discredited Norway
“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t,” Trump told supporters at a rally in Syracuse, New York. He added that the snub was “just another sign of how Norway and all these others are ripping off our country”.
Trump called Pillay a “mystery person” and “a liberal person who works at the United Nations, who nobody has ever heard of” during ‌the campaign rally. “I never heard of the person. Nobody did … I know a lot of people. I’ve never heard of this particular person. But congratulations anyway.”

articles.title_orig: Christa Pike out of hospital and back in prison after botched execution attempt
articles.title_zh: Christa Pike out of hospital and back in prison after botched execution attempt
articles.content_orig:
The Death Penalty Information Centre says she is the first person to live after receiving lethal injection drugs during an execution
Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee’s attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has been moved back to prison, her lawyers said on Saturday.
Pike, 50, was discharged from the hospital and is back at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Centre, the women’s prison where she was housed for 30 years, her lawyers said in a written statement.
“She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances. She is continuing to receive medical care at the prison, and we will continue to track her recovery,” the statement said.

articles.title_orig: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
articles.title_zh: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
articles.content_orig:
A shop also had its roof torn off in Milton, Florida
Four people have died and hundreds of thousands are without power after Hurricane Isaias battered parts of the southern US with powerful winds and heavy rain.
Officials reported two deaths each in the states of Alabama and Florida, which included people who were killed when trees fell on their houses.
At least 600,000 people were without power in several states as of Saturday afternoon, according to tracker PowerOutage.
Isaias made landfall in Florida late on Friday with maximum sustained winds of 105mph (168km/h) before being downgraded to a post-tropical cyclone.
The storm felled trees and ripped the roofs off buildings. Alabama, Florida and Georgia all declared states of emergency ahead of its arrival, while both Florida and Alabama issued mandatory evacuation orders to thousands of people.
The roof was blown off an apartment complex in Milton, Florida
Two deaths were reported in Florida's Escambia County. A woman was killed when a tree fell on her house, local Sheriff Chip Simmons said.
Joey Williams told NewsNation his wife had died in the storm. He said they went outside to snap pictures of the damage but, when they went back into their home, a tree fell through the roof and trapped them.
"I was able to squeeze out. My wife didn't make it," Williams told the outlet.
Simmons later reported that a man had died from carbon monoxide poisoning after running a generator in a garage that was not properly ventilated. Four other people who were in the same house were taken to hospital.
Officials had to rescue people in vehicles that became submerged by floodwaters. The Florida National Guard shared pictures of a truck stuck in a flood ditch, saying soldiers "stopped, swam to the vehicle and pulled its occupants to safety".
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis said flooding was a continued risk and warned of a "very hazardous situation".
In Florida, the storm tore through houses
The canopy of a petrol station collapsed in Gulf Breeze, Florida
In neighbouring Alabama, a sheriff was injured when a tree fell on him as he was responding to a car crash.
"Unfortunately, we have also learned that two Alabamians have lost their lives," Governor Kay Ivey said in a post on X, without giving further details on the circumstances of the deaths.
She also said officials were concerned about "spinoff tornadoes" in the state from the strong winds and heavy rain.
"As we approach the weekend and any travel plans, make sure you have reliable information as conditions develop," she said.
In Charleston, South Carolina, officials asked people to stay home on Saturday night as high tide is expected to reach 7.5ft (2.3m).
"After dark, floodwater is much harder to see and it's impossible to judge how deep it is from behind the wheel," the city said.
The storm is expected to continue to weaken as it travels to the north-east, but the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) warned that the Carolinas and Georgia could see floods from up to 10 inches (25cm) of rainfall.
In addition to Isaias, Tropical Storm Rachel is expected to hit southern California later on Saturday, and Hurricane Simon will hit the Pacific coast of Mexico on Sunday.
Hurricane Isaias was the first hurricane in the Atlantic's hurricane season, which largely has been delayed due to El NiÃ±o conditions in the Pacific.
Residents have begun removing felled trees

articles.title_orig: Man hospitalized after being struck by vehicle driven by ICE agent during chase on Clay Road in NW Harris County, HCSO says
articles.title_zh: Man hospitalized after being struck by vehicle driven by ICE agent during chase on Clay Road in NW Harris County, HCSO says
articles.content_orig:
A vehicle driven by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents hit and injured a man in the greater Houston area on Saturday, the Harris County Sheriff's Office said.
"The incident appears to have occurred while ICE authorities were conducting an enforcement action in the area," the sheriff's office said in a statement.
During a press conference, Major McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's special investigation bureau said the sheriff's office was called to the scene around 7:20 a.m.
ICE agents were headed south in pursuit of a wanted suspect, McConnell said, and the suspect drove west in an eastbound lane. The suspect bailed out of his vehicle and went on foot, he said.
The driver and passenger fled and ICE agents attempted to capture them both, he said. While trying to capture the passenger, the ICE agent hit him with his vehicle.
The victim was taken to a local hospital. McConnell said it appears the man has a broken leg, but no further details were given on the man's condition.
McConnell said the victim is a 48-year-old male and is currently in the custody of ICE at the hospital.
CBS News reached out to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security for more information.

articles.title_orig: Five DTF Printer Manufacturers in China to Know in 2026: Why After-Sales Support Should Lead the Supplier Decision
articles.title_zh: Five DTF Printer Manufacturers in China to Know in 2026: Why After-Sales Support Should Lead the Supplier Decision
articles.content_orig:
LINKO publishes a guide comparing Chinese DTF printer suppliers on service, consumables, and production for apparel decorators and print shops.
ZHUHAI, GUANGDONG, CHINA, October 10, 2026 / EINPresswire.com / -- LINKO , a Zhuhai-based manufacturer of DTF, UV DTF, DTG, and sublimation printing equipment, today published a buyer's guide for businesses sourcing Direct-to-Film (DTF) printers from China. The guide profiles five Chinese manufacturers and argues that after-sales support, more than machine price, decides whether a DTF printer stays productive after installation.
Why After-Sales Support Matters Most
A DTF printer is a production system: printheads, white ink circulation, film, powder, curing, and RIP software all have to work together. Most buyers install the machine thousands of kilometers from the factory, often with operators who are new to DTF. When a printhead clogs or colors shift, the speed and quality of the supplier's remote support decides whether a shop loses an hour or a week of production. For this reason, LINKO recommends that buyers evaluate service before specifications.
How the Five Manufacturers Were Selected
This is not a scored ranking. The companies below were chosen because each has an established DTF product line, a public export presence, and a registered business in China. LINKO is the publisher of this guide and is listed first for that reason. Buyers should verify every supplier independently.
LINKO (Zhuhai, Guangdong). Founded in 2008 and operated by Zhuhai Etro Technology Co., Ltd., LINKO has sites in Zhuhai and in Nansha District, Guangzhou, with around 160 staff, including 30 R&D engineers, and a stated production capacity of 180 to 200 units per month. Its range covers DTF printers, UV DTF printers, DTG printers, sublimation printers, auxiliary equipment, and consumables. The K-60 DTF printer is a 60 cm model configured with Epson i3200 printheads in 4- or 8-color setups.
LINKO's service model includes installation guidance, one-on-one operator training, free remote assistance, free sample printing, long-term spare parts and consumables supply, and a 12-month warranty on the mainboard, printhead board, and motor. The company serves more than 7,500 customers in over 100 countries through a service network covering 62 countries and regions, and has supported more than 600 overseas companies in starting or expanding printing businesses. On Trustpilot, LINKO's profile shows a TrustScore of 4.4 with all 10 published reviews rated five stars as of October 2026; reviewers from Germany and Finland describe fast replies and continued help until technical issues were resolved. Its DTF ink is OEKO-TEX ECO PASSPORT certified and REACH compliant, and its printers carry CE and RoHS certificates.
Tophee (Suzhou, Jiangsu). Suzhou Tophee Tech Co., Ltd. focuses on compact 30 cm (A3) DTF printers with two Epson XP600 or i1600 printheads, aimed at small studios and businesses starting with low-volume transfer printing.
HPRT (Xiamen, Fujian). Known first for thermal printing products, HPRT has expanded into DTF and digital textile equipment and sells through an international distribution network.
DGI (Shenzhen, Guangdong). A wide-format and industrial inkjet manufacturer whose DTF machines target commercial, production-oriented users.
Procolored (Shenzhen, Guangdong). A DTF and UV printer brand focused on compact and mid-size machines for small businesses and new print shops.
Five Checks Before Choosing a Supplier
1.	After-sales support: ask who answers technical questions, in which languages and time zones, how fast, and whether remote video support and operator training are included in the price. 2.	Independent reviews: read third-party reviews on platforms such as Trustpilot, and look at how the supplier handled problems, not just the star rating. 3.	Spare parts and consumables: confirm that printheads, dampers, boards, ink, film, and powder are kept in stock and can be shipped quickly. 4.	Printhead and width: match print width and printhead model, for example Epson i1600 or i3200, to daily output targets, and ask for speed figures with the pass mode stated. 5.	Factory and compliance: confirm the business license and factory address, and request OEKO-TEX, REACH, or MSDS documents for inks, film, and powder.
"Most buyers compare DTF printers on price, but what keeps a shop profitable is how quickly problems are fixed after the machine arrives," said Ted of LINKO's Customer Service Department. "We encourage buyers to read independent reviews of every supplier, including us, and to ask exactly what support they will get in the first year."
As more apparel brands move to on-demand and short-run production, demand is shifting toward wider printers, multi-head configurations, and integrated powder and curing units. These systems are more productive but also more complex, which makes supplier support a larger part of the total cost of ownership.
Founded in 2008 in Zhuhai, China, LINKO (Zhuhai Etro Technology Co., Ltd.) is a high-tech enterprise that develops and manufactures digital industrial printing equipment, including DTF printers, UV DTF printers, DTG printers, sublimation printers, and consumables. The company provides software, installation guidance, operator training, and technical support, and serves more than 7,500 customers in over 100 countries.

articles.title_orig: Navarre, Gulf Breeze residents assess storm damage from Hurricane Isaias
articles.title_zh: Navarre, Gulf Breeze residents assess storm damage from Hurricane Isaias
articles.content_orig:
NAVARRE, Fla. ( WALA ) - Residents across the Navarre and Gulf Breeze area spent the day after the storm assessing damage, clearing debris and checking on neighbors.
Navarre Beach survives with minimal damage
As darkness still hung over the Florida Panhandle Saturday morning, Navarre Beach was a virtual ghost town. Residents had evacuated, left with the question of what they would find when they returned.
With daylight, it became clear the area was spared the worst of the storm. Homes were missing siding and had other superficial damage but appeared structurally sound.
Navarre Beach Fire Rescue Fire Chief, Jonathan Kanzigg was out early surveying damage.
“I am ecstatic about how the island looks right now. I had anticipated not being able to move a fire truck on the island which would inhibit our response, but the roads are good. I haven’t seen any structural damage to houses. A lot of superficial...roofs, siding, garage doors. Some houses won’t be inhabitable, but structurally everything looks amazing,” Kanzigg said.
Gulf Breeze, Milton see more severe damage
Damage was more severe to the west. On Highway 98 near Gulf Breeze, campers at Camping World were overturned by strong north winds from the back side of the storm’s eye wall, with one coming close to the highway. Convoys of tree trimming and debris removal crews mobilized in the area. Officials said the area took a significant hit from the western eye wall, with strong north winds downing fences and trees.
Bergren Road was covered in fallen pine trees. Leslie Holcombe spent the morning cutting out trees there and near her home in Milton, where she said the damage looked different.
“We can definitely see what look like tornado tracks up in Milton over and over. Lots of trees down, roofs gone,” Holcombe said.
Neighbors help clear roads
Mark Bergman was cutting a tree out of the roadway so he could check on his home.
“Multiple trees down along Bergren, so I had a chainsaw in my car in preparation for this just in case, to cut my way back, so we’ve been cutting our way through here on Bergren Road and then, a couple of folks from Milton have been here as well, helping cut the trees down and now we’ve got the Santa Rosa County Sheriff here about to pull this tree out of the way with a winch,” Bergman said.
Asked whether people were coming together, Bergman said, “Yeah, they’re coming together. Everyone’s pitching in, taking care of each other which is what it’s all about.”
State crews assist with cleanup
State crews with the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission arrived to help finish clearing trees and reopen the neighborhood.
Public and government agencies worked together through the day to begin restoring the area on the way to recovery.

articles.title_orig: Police call Erie mass shooting a 'horrific scene' after 9 found dead, including 2 small children
articles.title_zh: Police call Erie mass shooting a 'horrific scene' after 9 found dead, including 2 small children
articles.content_orig:
Crime scene tape still surrounds the home where eight people tragically lost their lives in a mass shooting Friday.
Officers were called to Erie's East Side just before 5 p.m. after a report of two women shot outside the Perry Street home.
Authorities say before they were shot, they were outside the home, pounding on the door. When the door open, the 45-year-old gunman, who was a family member of seven people killed, shot the two women.
Officials say police were at the scene minutes after receiving a ShotSpotter alert, however by that time all victims were already dead.
Among the dead, a woman who was pregnant, two young children and a family friend.
Video Below: Press conference from Rick Lorah
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah told WJET, our ABC affiliate in Erie , repeatedly that the number of lives lost at the 700 block of Perry Street was not only devastating but the crime scene was by far the worst one he has ever seen in his law enforcement career.
After the shooting of the two women, the gunman was seen running into a nearby home.
Officers surrounded the home before forcing their way inside after securing a warrant.
Once inside, officials say "officers were met with an eerie silence." Police found multiple bodies, including the bodies of a 5-year-old boy and a 1-year-old girl.
Authorities say the two young children were both found on the first floor of the home, while the rest of the victims were found in a second-floor stairwell.
The victims in that stairwell included the 24-year-old woman who was 8 months pregnant when she was killed.
That gunman was also found dead from what officials believe to be a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
“Our hearts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected by this tragedy. There are no words that can be adequately expressed the magnitude of the loss of life here,” said Chief Lorah.
Original coverage of the shooting below:
”Yeah, it’s a horrific scene,” replied Lorah. “There was a large loss of life inside that residence and outside that residence.” Lorah then went on to say, "I can tell you that this is a tragic, tragic situation.”
An investigation into what led to the shooting is still ongoing.
Gov. Josh Shapiro is among the many offering condolences following Friday evening's mass shooting.
"I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians. My heart breaks for this family. Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community," Shapiro posted on X.
Republican Rep. Mike Kelly also released a statement, saying he was praying for the Erie community after the devastating events in Erie.
"May we hold the victims, their families, and those impacted by this tragedy in our hearts," Kelly said, in part.

articles.title_orig: Stephen King and His ‘King Whisperer’ Resurrect ‘Carrie’
articles.title_zh: Stephen King and His ‘King Whisperer’ Resurrect ‘Carrie’
articles.content_orig:
[Warning: The following contains spoilers for the Season 1 finale of Carrie . Read at your own risk!]
If you've seen all eight episodes of Prime Video's Carrie , then you know that the finale played out as one would expect a Carrie adaptation to, at least in the broad sense. Yes, pig's blood was dumped on the title character at prom, and yes, a massacre followed, thanks to Carrie White's immense telekinetic powers.
…Except there were some rather huge changes too, as Mike Flanagan 's version of Carrie was a major reinterpretation and modernizing of Stephen King 's novel. Not only did Flanagan expand the story across an entire school semester and offer bold new spins on Carrie ( Summer H. Howell ) and Margaret White ( Samantha Sloyan ), he also included several other women with telekinetic powers — something King did say existed in his novel, but without bringing them into his story. And oh yeah, there was one other big change… Carrie lived at the end!
Rather than dying in the wake of all the carnage she'd left, as she did in King's book and the 1976 film adaptation, Carrie ends the season driving off to parts unknown with Emaline ( Thalia Dudek ), a more seasoned woman with powers. Earlier, Emaline had "taken the wheel" from Carrie at the prom, taking control of her body, with Carrie's permission, arguably becoming the one who actually is to blame for most of the deaths that followed — though there are some notable exceptions.
We talked to Carrie's creator and cast about the full season, the show's future, and more.
Everything you need for fall TV:
So at what point in developing Carrie did Flanagan and his collaborators decide that Carrie would survive? As Flanagan explained to TV Guide, "We knew it from the get-go," noting that once he decided he wanted to bring in other women with telekinetic powers — something King would delve into himself in subsequent work — that helped guide a lot of what followed.
King, an executive producer on Carrie , has made it known that he's a fan of Flanagan's previous adaptations of his work. Flanagan recalled speaking to King about his ideas for the project and let him know that "One of the things that I was really excited about is that the novel talks about Carrie's place in this long legacy of gifted women. But in every other version, she's never lived long enough to realize that she wasn't alone, and that was an opportunity for real change. And that was something that Stephen King was excited about too."
Flanagan recalled telling King, "Look, you point explicitly at this larger universe in the book, and we never see it. It never comes to bear on her story. Can we fold that in? Can we see the tip of this iceberg?" He added that with those changes in place, "This is a story about her coming into her own and stepping out of this house she's lived her whole life into the bigger world."
Of course, whether or not we actually see where Carrie goes next depends on if the series is renewed or not. But as for what Howell hopes to see happen next for Carrie, should she get to continue on with the character, the actress said, "I want her to find herself, because I think we end the series where she's very confused and traumatized and ridden with guilt, and just not in a good place like she was at the start. It's ironic that she starts out more confident and happy being home, and then the outside world tears that all away. So it'd be nice to see her come back to that more and to find her light again."
Flanagan sure seemed to be hinting at a brighter future, stating that with the ending, "I wanted to see her heading out, going away from all of this and having to decide who she's going to be now that she knows what she's capable of." Flanagan has previously said he envisions Carrie as a three-season series, if he's able to continue it, and remarked, "The story just felt, in so many ways, like a first act. It was like, yeah, I want to see her alive at the end of this! And Stephen King was very, very supportive of that."
As to whether Flanagan has specific plans in mind already for where he'd like to take a second season, the showrunner said, "Yeah, there are ideas, but honestly I was focused entirely on making sure we survived this season, and just got to a place where if we cut to black at the end of Episode 8, and that's all we ever see of this version, that we've honored that story and we've completed Carrie's [season] arc. That was my priority. There are absolutely possibilities, and I certainly would be lying if I said I wasn't thinking about them, but our priority was kind of to get through this, see how it's received, and then go from there."
Though Carrie lives, Margaret White does not, although her death plays out differently than in the book or other adaptations. When the White house collapses on Carrie and Margaret, Margaret is revealed to have telekinetic abilities of her own — albeit ones she's barely ever tapped into. Though Margaret survives this event, soon after, she is coldly killed by the mysterious Adelaide ( Kate Siegel ), the leader of the group of telekinetic women who were tracking Carrie all season, after Margaret admits she likely would not be able to access those abilities again. As Adelaide says, "A lot of people have a little bit of Shine and they don't even know it," with Flanagan getting in a mention of The Shining , used as an overarching term in King's universe for those with mental powers.
While the book mentions Margaret's grandmother had telekinesis, Flanagan is the first to have Margaret herself display this ability, which we learn she once used as a child, only to suppress it afterwards. This puts her relationship with Carrie, and her reaction to what she's seeing her daughter do — which began when an upset Carrie makes rocks fall onto their house when she's a child — in a new light, given she'd be seeing something she at least partially recognized.
Observed Sloyan, of this revelation, "I think it allows us to understand, if you go back to the beginning, why she's so convinced that her daughter's in danger. It's because she believes this is real, and I think from the moment that we see the rocks hitting the house, she makes the decision 'Carrie's never leaving this home, because I don't know what she's capable of.'"
She added, "Margaret's such a control freak, and to have something that she felt was so uncontrolled within herself, it's like she's trying to squash it."
Arthur Conti and Alison Thornton, Carrie
Carrie's tormentor, Chris Hargensen ( Alison Thornton ), meanwhile has a similar ending as in the book, as she and her boyfriend, Billy Nolan ( Arthur Conti ), are killed inside Billy's car by Carrie's abilities, after the two were the ones who poured pig's blood on Carrie at the prom. In this moment, it's made clear Carrie herself is the one responsible for this much more personal death, as she flips their  car off the road and then crushes the car in with her abilities to flatten Billy first, and then Chris.
Said Thornton, "That was one of my favorite moments to film. It was like 3:00 a.m. It was one of the last things we shot that day, and I remember walking up to the car, and Mike came up to me, and he said, 'You know, I think Chris knows that it's the end.'"
Thornton recalled telling Flanagan that she agreed, and that Flanagan replied, "'Take all the time you need, and I will see you on the other side.' And it was just the most beautiful piece of direction that he could have given me."
Thornton's Chris is more nuanced than previous incarnations, as we meet her in a better, friendlier place, only to see her turn into the worst version of herself as her own life begins to fall apart. She goes on to make terrible, harmful decisions, one of which is dating the dangerous Billy, who encourages all of her worst impulses. Her final words to Carrie, seconds before she's killed, are "I'm sorry," and Thornton remarked, "I think I said 'I'm sorry' three times, and to me, it was like, in that mome

US president says agreement needed to lower fuel prices, but move likely to create fresh crisis with Ukraine and Nato allies
Donald Trump is on a fresh collision course with Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European allies after his stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel upended years of US and western pressure on the Kremlin to end its war against Ukraine.
Zelenskyy reacted furiously to Trump’s announcement of the deal with Vladimir Putin on Friday, calling it “absolutely terrible” and “not fair and not honest”.
The Ukrainian president said “back room deals” with the Russian leader would give Putin more chances on the battlefield. On Saturday morning, Ukrainian officials reported that a Russian attack had killed 12 people in the south-east, including three children, and Moscow claimed its troops were advancing in the east.
In a move likely to create a fresh crisis with Washington’s Nato allies, Trump announced the deal with Putin on his Truth Social network, saying it was essential to reduce fuel prices in the US, which have soared as a result of his decision to go to war against Iran.
“I have just concluded a highly successful discussion with President Vladimir Putin , of Russia,” he said, to deliver millions of tonnes of diesel fuel over the next few months.
He added: “Diesel prices for Americans and, indeed, the world, will be COMING DOWN, IN RECORD NUMBERS, AND FAST! Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my greatest priority.”
Fuel prices have soared since Iran closed the strait of Hormuz, a strategically sensitive choke point that was the passageway for 20% of global oil supplies before the war. While costs have risen for motorists – a gallon of regular fuel in the US is about $4.20 (£3.17) – it is the price of diesel, which last month hit a record high of $6.52, that has inflicted the most damage on Trump and the Republicans as November’s midterm elections approach.
Diesel is the main supply chain fuel, and a rise in its costs feeds into consumer prices and also hurts US farmers, who need it to operate machinery.
Democrats said the agreement undercut a law Trump signed last month allowing for a broad range of sanctions on Russian banks, officials and tankers, as well as directing him to impose steep tariffs on the top five importers of oil or natural gas from Russia. The law gave Trump wide discretion to make exceptions to its provisions.
“This is what failure looks like. Failure for President Trump to live up to his promises to lower costs for Americans. Failure to protect America from its adversaries,” said a statement from the Senate Democratic leader, Chuck Schumer, Senator Jeanne Shaheen, who is the top Democrat on the foreign relations committee, and Senator Elizabeth Warren, the ranking Democrat on the banking committee.
Some Republicans also criticised the agreement.
“Propping up Putin’s war economy is morally wrong as he uses that money to bomb cities,” congressman Don Bacon, a Nebraska Republican, wrote on X . “The President’s policies towards Russia and Ukraine are failures. We need moral clarity not moral ambiguity.”
Zelenskyy told Axios that it “looks like a happy birthday present for Putin. It looks absolutely terrible.” The Russian leader turned 74 this week.
In a long social media post, Zelenskyy, who has had an uneasy relationship with Trump, said the deal amounted to “an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged”. Russia was likely to repay it with “further terror and perfidy”.
“It plays into Russia’s hands – allowing it to kill more, wage war for longer, have even less respect for America, and inflict even greater losses and damage on the world,” he said.
Referring on Saturday to the attack on the south-eastern city of Zaporizhzhia that killed 12 people, Zelenskyy wrote on X: “Today, Russia expressed its thanks for the lifting of sanctions on diesel exports by dropping five glide bombs on residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia.
“Last night confirmed once again that in Russia, they take any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they can keep dropping bombs on cities. Different signals are needed.”
​ Separately, Russian media cited the defence ⁠ministry ⁠​as saying its forces ⁠had ​captured ‌the ‌settlements of Lukashove ‌and Lobanivka in Ukraine’s​ eastern ‌Kharkiv region.
​ Zelenskyy previously said Putin had been playing games with Trump, and on Saturday, a Kremlin spokesperson said the Russian leader had responded with “understanding” to Trump’s proposals to de-escalate the conflict.
Trump announced the diesel deal as his envoys, Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner, met Ukrainian and European officials in Miami to discuss proposals to end the war.
Zelenskyy, in a separate statement released by Ukraine’s embassy in Washington on Friday, said the Ukrainian negotiators had been “used as a smokescreen for the deal”, which he called “a weak decision by strong partners”.
“That is certainly not fair. It is certainly not how partners should treat each other,” he said.
Trump recently criticized Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries, calling on Zelenskyy to choose alternative targets. The Ukrainian leader rejected the request unless Russia stopped attacking Ukraine’s energy infrastructure.
Tensions have been rising between Russia and European Nato members amid speculation that Moscow might be preparing military action intended to test the alliance’s resolve.
The latest development is likely to worsen Zelenskyy’s relationship with the Trump administration . He was infamously ambushed by Trump and the vice-president, JD Vance, last year in an explosive White House encounter when the president told him: “You don’t have the cards.”
But Trump has since reportedly grown disenchanted with Putin, expressing disappointment at his failure to reach a peace deal.
Trump’s willingness to reach a fuel agreement with Putin comes despite Russia’s support for Iran in its war with the US. Russia is believed to have given Iran satellite intelligence and overhead surveillance data detailing the locations of US forces, ships, aircraft and military bases. It has also provided drone components and ammunition.

articles.title_orig: The 2026 CFMOTO SR-S750: Riding China's attempt at a Japanese sportsbike
articles.title_zh: The 2026 CFMOTO SR-S750: Riding China's attempt at a Japanese sportsbike
articles.content_orig:
I was set to hate it. I felt I had to. It was made in China, and while I think CFMoto, on general principles, makes pretty good bikes, what business does it have attempting an in-line four? That engine configuration is the stuff of legend. The Chinese want to splash in that pond, they wanna bring their A-game.
The SR-S was indeed an in-line four, and I’d sharpened my fangs on in-line fours back when they breathed fire, hailed Satan, and tank-slapped their way to red-line.
I kept riding in-line fours after the Japanese engineered the tank-slapping out of them, and their unique shriek will always be one of the great songs of my people. Nothing assaults your ears and screams “Fast” like an in-line four being hammered through the gears.
It all began in 1969 with the Honda CB750-Four, the bike that started the so-called superbike era. The prototype was unveiled in 1968 at the Tokyo Motor Show, and the first production bikes arrived in the USA the following year. Kawasaki upped the ante when it unveiled its 900cc Z1 in 1972…and away we all went.
In-line fours got bigger, went a hell of a lot faster, and schooled several generations of riders in sheer terror, while simultaneously addicting them to industrial doses of adrenaline. And jail.
Around the turn of the century, it was decided that 1000cc was kinda the right capacity for an in-line four superbike, and while Suzuki flirted with a 1400cc in-line four from 2011 to 2008, that fat bastard was never a contender for the superbike crown. Suzuki was alright about that. It also produced what many still believe to be the finest in-line four ever made – the K5-engined GSX-R1000 – which was itself the obvious performance progression of the just-as-legendary GSX-R750, the bike that defined “handling” 25 years ago. Suzuki figured it would just jam its 1000cc monster engine into that wickedly agile 750cc bastard to see if it danced.
It did. But to many people, the GSX-R750 still danced just that little bit better. The 1000 went harder, but the 750 handled sharper. That was the argument. And the argument was ultimately settled by the market. Suzuki stopped making the GSX-R750 in 2016, but it was essentially the same bike it had made in 2011. The GSX-R750 was still being sold in the USA up until 2019, but that was just unsold 2016 stock.
The in-line 1000 had won out. Size mattered, it seemed.
But ask anyone who has ever ridden the GSX-R750 and the GSX-R1000 which one handled better, and they will tell you it was the 750. It was always the 750.
We now live in a world where in-line fours are all 1000cc track monsters, and the market all seems to be about parallel twins – the sensible cardigan of the motorcycle world.
Older riders, who once sold important organs to buy in-line fours, are now too old and too scared to even care what 14,000rpm in top means on an in-line four. Younger riders are far too risk-averse and have been bludgeoned by legislation and the policing that goes with it to even think about red-lining an in-line four in all six gears.
So why the Hell would CFMoto produce an all-new four-cylinder in-line 750? It was going great guns with its parallel twin offerings. They were incredible bang-for-your buck, improving with each model run, and absolutely making the big Japanese Four sit up and pay attention.
Why this four-cylinder winged thing, with its strange rear wheel, and cutting-edge suite of electronic whizz-bangery?
No idea, and I could care less. Maybe the Chinese are just throwing this 750 SR-S out there to see what would happen. Maybe they wanted to make the Japanese crazy. Maybe it was a little of both.
Utkarsh was very kind when he first wrote about this bike, but then Utkarsh is young, full of hope, open of mind and burdened with a sweet disposition. I am not, and I was determined to hate it.
And then I saw it in the flesh and thought: that’s not too bad, actually. Sure, the rear wheel looks like it’s meant to slice giant potatoes, but close inspection revealed those munted inserts could be removed with an Allen key and thrown into the sea.
The rest of it looked cool. Very cool. But I was certain it was not going to be a GSX-R750 when I rode it. And I was right. It was not. It was a very long way away from Suzuki’s epic sportsbike statement.
CFMoto’s SR-S is a very different statement. Sure, you hit the starter button and it instantly fires into that intoxicating angry beehive hum only an in-line four can make. I remember looking at it after I started it up and muttering: “Well, you certainly sound like you mean business…”
And it did, but it was a different kind of business. It was a business for our time. A gentler, friendlier, easier-to-ride kinda business, because we live in just such a world – or we’d like to. Or the government would like us to. So the SR-S is not the GSX-R.
For starters, there is no racer’s crouch happening here. You sit canted forward, but not in a way that puts all your weight on your arms and forces your neck back. Think sports-tourer rather than sportsbike.
It seemed to handle well, but it was shod with Maxxis SP tyres, and I could not bring myself to see how they dealt with me at Max Stupid. I’m funny about tyres. Most people are. There are brands you like and trust and there are brands you don’t. I have had nothing to do with Maxxis. I read good things about them, but the Internet is full of lies.
Ridden at a few degrees less than Max Stupid, they seemed fine. I left it at that. The SR-S tipped in sweetly and held its line – and crucially, it did not lash out viciously when you gassed it on hard. Yes, this was certainly no GSX-R750. It didn’t seem to be strangled performance-wise. It just wasn’t angry.
Looking at the numbers, it made sense. The CF‑Moto SR‑S750 makes 110 hp with 80 Nm of torque and weighs 213 kg, while the Suzuki GSX‑R750 makes 148 hp, has 86.3 Nm and weighs 190 kg. The wheelbase and rake comparisons are also revealing. The SR-S is 1419mm long and the GSX-R is 1390mm long. Their respective rakes are 24.5 degrees and 24.6 degrees.
That there should tell you everything you need to know about why it’s not a GSX-R750. The SR-S is a slower-steering, slightly pudgier, and markedly less powerful bike than the legendary GSX-R750.
But then it’s not trying to be one of those. Those days are gone. The people who wanted those numbers, or told themselves they did, are no more. The SRE-S is very much an in-line four 750 for our time.
It is as modern as drone warfare. There is no key. There is no fob. There is a small black plastic thing a third the size of a credit card with which you touch a place on the inside left of the fairing. Then all its lights come on in a celebration of electric modernity. I hated that wee plastic thingy. I am guaranteed to lose such a starting gimmick.
I hate fobs too. They solved a problem no-one was having. I can spend three days riding through rivers, jumping into oceans, and being rained on, and my bike key will still start my bike. My fob won’t. My key does not require batteries. My fob does.
The SR-S750s starting “card” has no battery, and it may well work if I leave it in the sink overnight, so it may be an improvement on the fob. But I am primitively confident that whatever sorcery makes it speak to the fairing will, at the worst possible time, cease to speak to the fairing.
But young people will love it. Technology does not mortify them like it does me. And they will be pleased you can also lock and unlock the thing with a password, Bluetooth, or via the CFMOTO RIDE app. There is also a three-way electric lock that does your steering, seat, and petrol cap.
Once all the lights come on and you start it and are greeted with that lovely deep engine hum, riding it is a doddle. And it’s so smooth, like Chinese silk. This is no small thing. In-line fours all had a certain amount of handlebar “buzz” in them. It used to be hand and mind-numbing, but it got better as time went by, and then only really bothered people up near red-line. Th

articles.title_orig: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
articles.title_zh: Exasperation and Resignation in Greece Over Allegations Against Kimberly Guilfoyle
articles.content_orig:
In a normal political environment, this would be about the time the ambassador scheduled a one-way flight out of Athens.
Donald Trump didn’t need another round of foreign policy problems, but it’s clear the president’s ambassadors are creating difficult complications for his administration. One ambassador in particular, however, stands out — and not in a good way.
The Wall Street Journal reported a couple of weeks ago on Kimberly Guilfoyle, a former Fox News contributor who is also Donald Trump Jr.’s former fiancée, and her controversial tenure as the U.S. ambassador to Greece. Among the more problematic aspects of her work has been Guilfoyle’s involvement of lobbyist Christos Marafatsos in so many official meetings “that some foreign officials mistook him for her chief of staff.”
The same report added that the U.S. ambassador has promoted Marafatsos’ employer, Greek construction firm Aktor Group, for energy deals, to the puzzlement of officials in the region and to the concern of key congressional Democrats .
This week, however, new allegations made her situation vastly more serious. The Wall Street Journal also reported :
Kimberly Guilfoyle was preparing for her congressional hearing to become U.S. ambassador to Greece when she reached out to a Trump donor with an urgent request: She needed $100,000 that she said she owed American Express — in a way that wouldn’t leave a paper trail.
“It won’t show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express,” she wrote on Signal, according to messages reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. “Please.”
According to the reporting, which has not been independently verified by MS NOW, Guilfoyle had been in communication with Eric Deters, a failed former Republican congressional candidate, who was hoping for the Trump administration’s assistance on some personal tax and legal issues.
He was reportedly prepared to pay Guilfoyle as much as $1 million if she helped use her influence within Team Trump to make her troubles go away, and she assured him that she could deliver.
“Every secretary of you know defense, transportation, treasury commerce IRS commissioner everyone gets right back to me,” she wrote in a message to Deters, adding, “Oh yeah, l’m forgetting cash Patel,” in an apparent misspelling of FBI Director Kash Patel’s name.
But in early July, the then-nominee apparently wanted an advance.
“Honey please I need you to get this done for me today,” she texted Deters, adding a prayer hands emoji and a PDF with bill payment instructions from American Express. “You could just send it here,” she wrote on July 3, 2025, just days before her July 9 confirmation hearing.
Deters ultimately declined the request, although the Journal’s report went on to note that Guilfoyle also expressed concern about their communications potentially reaching the public.
In one especially memorable exchange, Guilfoyle warned him not to reference money or payments by way of texts: “Eric, I really wish you would stop papering all these things.”
In context, “papering” apparently meant “putting controversial comments in writing.”
In another exchange, Deters suggested he was not altogether impressed with the return on his investment.
“I have paid you $300,000 over the years,” he wrote to Guilfoyle. “As of this memo, I have not received one favor. I am not naive or a sucker. I need results.”
A lawyer for Guilfoyle said the ambassador disputed the authenticity of the messages obtained by the newspaper, but he declined to provide specifics. Deters told the Journal, “She never came through on anything.”
In a normal political environment, this would be about the time the ambassador might decide to update her resume and schedule a one-way flight out of Athens.
Asked about the revelations, Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska told MS NOW, “If true, it is bad.” Another House GOP member, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, added, “This is the type of crap that will cost us the majority.”
Q: Do you have any reaction to a US ambassador asking someone to pay off debt in exchange for access to other government officials?VANCE: Well, so — with that hypothetical, obviously I don't love that, but I, you know, I don't know exactly who you're talking about, I don't know the full details
JD Vance was also asked about the reporting at an unrelated press conference on Thursday morning.
“Well, so, with that hypothetical, obviously I don’t love that, but I, you know, I don’t know exactly who you’re talking about, I don’t know the full details,” the vice president replied.
With 26 days remaining in the midterm election cycle and Democrats already focusing heavily on corruption allegations surrounding the Republican administration, Guilfoyle’s controversy couldn’t have come at a worse time for Team Trump or the GOP.
UPDATE (October 8, 2026, 11:52 a.m. ET): During an on-air appearance with MS NOW’s Peter Alexander on Thursday morning, Deters said, “I cannot stand Kimberly Guilfoyle. Kimberly Guilfoyle is a wicked evil person. She thought I was going to be a sucker, and I’m not a sucker.”
In the same interview, Deters added that his previous arrangement with Guilfoyle was “absolutely … a quid pro quo.”
Steve Benen is a producer for "The Rachel Maddow Show," the editor of MaddowBlog and an MS NOW political contributor. He's also the bestselling author of "Ministry of Truth: Democracy, Reality, and the Republicans' War on the Recent Past."

articles.title_orig: 8 People Are Killed in Shooting in Erie, Pa., City Officials Say
articles.title_zh: 8 People Are Killed in Shooting in Erie, Pa., City Officials Say
articles.content_orig:
ERIE, Pa. — Nine people, including at least two children, are dead following a shooting near E. 7th and Perry streets in the City of Erie Friday night, investigators confirmed Saturday.
The suspected shooter was among those found dead inside a home at 722 Perry St. Police said there is no ongoing threat to the public.
The City of Erie said Saturday that all nine deaths occurred before officers arrived at the scene, clarifying earlier reports surrounding the timeline of the incident.
Police responded within minutes after receiving a ShotSpotter alert. Officers initially had limited information about what had happened, including whether the suspected shooter remained inside the home or continued to pose a threat.
Two women were found dead outside the residence. Investigators later discovered additional victims inside the home, including children.
Erie police and the department’s SWAT team surrounded the residence as officers worked to determine what had happened and sought a search warrant.
The city said no additional gunshots were fired after police arrived. Sounds heard during the tactical response that may have been mistaken for gunfire were actually flash bangs used by law enforcement.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah described the scene Friday night as one of the most difficult and heartbreaking his officers and investigators have encountered.
“The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing,” Lorah said.
Mayor Daria Devlin also called the incident a “terrible tragedy.”
“Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone impacted by tonight’s tragedy,” Devlin said Friday night.
Police have not yet released the identities of those killed or discussed a possible motive.
The city said additional details about the shootings and the police response will be released during a news conference scheduled for 4 p.m. Saturday. Erie News Now will stream the news conference live on-air and online.
Police and the Erie County Coroner’s Office continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
The city is also directing anyone affected by the tragedy who would like to speak with a crisis counselor to Crisis Services at 814-456-2014.
Stay with Erie News Now for the latest information as it becomes available.

articles.title_orig: Educators using food to teach science, social studies
articles.title_zh: Educators using food to teach science, social studies
articles.content_orig:
Live updates all day, breaking news as it happens and weather every 10 minutes
Beyond serving as a spooky decoration, pumpkin is a nutrient-dense addition to your diet that offers several health benefits. Pumpkin is extremely versatile, thanks to its natural sweetness, which works well in desserts as well as savoury dishes. Rich in antioxidants, pumpkins can help neutr…
CHICAGO — At least once a month, Rita Leary incorporates food into a science lesson at Ashburn Community Elementary School. On a recent Thursday, it was all about honey.
The goal was to conduct a sensory exploration of honey samples native to Illinois, while hitting a core standard of food education: Food connects us, and the food and the environment are interconnected.
Leary’s lesson was sparked by Pilot Light, an organization founded in 2010 that developed a food-based curriculum for educators to integrate lessons about food, nutrition and the food system into everyday subjects like math, science and reading.
“It’s not like, ‘Oh here’s a carrot and here’s why carrots are good for you,’ but instead we use food to learn more about science,” said Leary. “Everybody likes food. And the students are so engaged, calm and so polite with each other.”
Teacher Rita Leary engages with her students during a Pilot Light food education lesson on Sept. 17 in her science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
In September, Pilot Light launched an update to its Food Education Center, a digital hub of free pre-K-12 lesson plans and resources. The nonprofit, which started in a single Chicago classroom with local chefs, now partners with administrators, schools and teachers in 26 states. It’s also launching its first chapter in New York City this fall.
Leary has been using a mix of self-made lessons and digital curriculum from the organization for more than five years. She wants more educators across Chicago Public Schools to find the benefit in incorporating food into classroom learning.
That Thursday, Leary’s sixth, seventh and eighth graders sat at their lab tables in groups of four, watching closely as their science teacher promised a tasting of pumpkin honey, apple blossom honey, blueberry honey and clover honey. Each flavor corresponds to the plant the bees pollinated, she reminded them.
But first — a few tests, for science.
Eighth grader Taylor White smells a honey sample during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Leary turned off the lights and asked her students to use mini flashlights to categorize the honey by shades. Then, to test each honey’s viscosity, the students flipped the vials over to see how quickly or slowly the honey flowed.
“Viscosity is thickness, how slow something flows — seventh graders, we’ll be talking about it a lot when we get to lava and volcanoes, because some lava is quite viscous,” Leary said.
Leary explained that when forager bees collect nectar from flowers, it’s almost 80% water. The worker bees fan their wings to make a phase change that turns it into that gooey honey texture.
Next, she asked the students to smell each sample.
“Oh my God, the pumpkin one smells like NyQuil, the honey NyQuil!” screeched Lia Henry, a seventh grader.
When it was finally time to taste each one, Henry confirmed that the dark-hued pumpkin honey tasted like NyQuil, too.
It was a “pretty cool” day in science class, seventh grader Tyjon Poole said, plus he never knew different kinds of honey could taste so unusual.
“If you really look and think about your tongue, it’s a map, right? All of those taste buds aren’t the same. They are chemical receptors, and they receive different kinds of chemicals,” Leary said, instructing the class to spread the honey on different corners of the tongue to experience the nuance in flavor.
Though the honey project was her own, Leary said if it wasn’t for Pilot Light, she may have never thought to incorporate food in her science lesson plan, because the public education system doesn’t necessarily require food education.
Science teacher Rita Leary teaches a Pilot Light food education lesson about bees and honey on Sept. 17 at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
“And it’s not always eating — the next one for the sixth graders, because they’re looking at plant and animal cells, we’re going to see what cooking does to the cell wall,” Leary said. “A few years ago, when I was teaching social studies, we had a chef visit us through Pilot Light, and he gave a presentation on spices that traveled to Spain through North Africa, and that fit right in with our medieval history unit.”
Pilot Light’s ultimate goal is to make food education a part of every child’s learning, said Alexandra DeSorbo-Quinn, the organization’s executive director.
“What are all the ways in which we connect with food? What do we need to know about food? What is it we can do once we have all this knowledge? We can make different decisions. We can advocate,” DeSorbo-Quinn said. “There’s a lot of different ways in which food connects to our lives. You can teach anything through food.”
Tyjon Poole stirs a sample of honey during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Getting the Food Education Center to where it is now was a heavy undertaking, driven by teachers who were part of focus groups that helped shape more than 200 lesson plans designed by a team of chefs, farmers, medical experts and psychologists.
The resources cover an array of topics, including agriculture, astronomy, historical events, ecosystems, geometry, global challenges, sustainability and food insecurity.
Pilot Light now reaches thousands of educators and classrooms, but it didn’t start that way.
During the Obama administration, First Lady Michelle Obama’s “Let’s Move!” campaign urged chefs to partner with K-12 schools to weave nutrition and food into everyday life. Some chefs also helped students build school gardens.
Before the plan materialized, Matthias Merges, chef and proprietor of hospitality group Folkart, was already working in classrooms at his daughter’s school, sharing insights about salmon farming, fish migration, how something goes from the ocean to someone’s plate and more. After he and other chefs went to Washington, D.C., for the launch of Michelle Obama’s “Chefs Move to Schools” program, they started to put a plan on paper.
Students in Rita Leary’s science class listen to a Pilot Light food education lesson about bees on Sept. 17 at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
Chefs took turns going to classrooms on select days, using food to teach a lesson on any given topic.
“We’d email our list of teachers and ask, ‘What do you happen to be teaching that day?’” said Jason Hammel, chef and owner of Lula Cafe in Logan Square. “When the emails came back, like one classroom was doing fractions. OK, that’s easy. We’ll make a pie and cut it up, or make a recipe. But then we got the Boston Tea Party, or plate tectonics, or how magnets work … the different chefs had to figure out a way to use food to teach (it).”
Recently at Ancona School in Kenwood, educator Christopher Weber brought together 80 elementary students, parents and teachers for a day of learning and cooking to fill their neighborhood’s Love Fridge with homemade soups and bread, with custom labels to promote allergy safety and raise awareness of food insecurity in their community.
Seventh grader Da’Sean Mackey tastes a honey sample during a Pilot Light food education class on Sept. 17 in Rita Leary’s science classroom at Ashburn Elementary School in Chicago.
At Langston Hughes Elementary in Roseland, STEM teacher LaTina Taylor spearheaded a project that became one of the most cherished stories within Pilot Light. articles.title_orig: 2 dead from storm as Isaias brings threat of flash floods across the Southeast
articles.title_zh: 2 dead from storm as Isaias brings threat of flash floods across the Southeast
articles.content_orig:
Isaias is now well inland over the Southeast but still has a threat of flooding rain, strong wind gusts and tornadoes in parts of the South and East through Sunday.
(MORE: Isaias maps tracker | live updates )
Hurricane Isaias made landfall Friday night in the Florida Panhandle at Category 2 strength.
Wind gusts over 110 mph were clocked in several panhandle locations, along with storm surge flooding. Over 700,000 customers are without power in its wake.
We have a full recap of the events leading up to landfall at the bottom of this article.
Isaias is now "post tropical," which just means that it has lost its tropical characteristics, but there is still heavy rain and gusty winds with its inland remnants.
Set The Weather Company as a 'Preferred Source' to get quicker access to the news you value.
You can see where the rain is currently in the map below, along with any flash flood or tornado watches and warnings.
( MORE: What all these tropical terms mean )
The biggest threat left from Isaias this weekend is a threat of flash flooding, particularly in parts of the Southeast Saturday.
The heaviest additional rain is expected through Saturday night in the foothills of the Appalachians from eastern and northern Georgia to upstate South Carolina, western North Carolina and western Virginia.
It's there where the flash flood threat is highest, especially in hilly or mountainous terrain.
Other areas of heavy rain that could lead to flash flooding include:
Wind gusts capable of at least some tree damage and additional power outages will continue through early Sunday in parts of the Southeast, particularly where high wind warnings are in effect, shown on the map below.
Some gusts in the Smoky Mountains could reach 60 to 70 mph.
Trees could also be toppled more easily in ground soaked by heavy rain.
There is a threat for severe thunderstorms and tornadoes across Georgia, the eastern Florida Panhandle and into the Carolinas Saturday and Saturday evening.
This is common with the remnants of former tropical storms and hurricanes.
That threat of isolated tornadoes and strong thunderstorm wind gusts continues Sunday in the East.
Be prepared for power outages across the Southeast that could last at least several hours or possibly multiple days in areas that were under hurricane warnings near the Gulf Coast.
Avoid flood-prone areas and never drive into flooded stretches of roads.
Stay out of areas near the Gulf Coast impacted by the hurricane until local officials give the all clear to return.
Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, Friday evening with sustained winds of 105 mph, a Category 2 hurricane.
The highest gust recorded was 116 mph in Santa Rosa Sound, Florida, where sustained winds of 91 mph were also measured.
Pensacola reported a 102-mph wind gust earlier Friday evening. Gulf Breeze, Florida, located across Pensacola Bay from Pensacola, reported a wind gust of 97 mph and sustained winds of 83 mph.
Isaias ( ees-ah-EE-ahs) is one of the trickier names to pronounce on this year's list. To hear the correct pronunciation, listen here .
Isaias replaced "Ike" on one of the Atlantic name lists after that name was retired following the destructive, deadly 2008 hurricane .
It wasn't used during its first year of eligibility in 2014, since we only reached the eighth name, Hanna, that year.
However, the name was used in 2020 for a storm that eventually tracked up the East Coast with destructive winds.
Around 11 a.m. CDT Friday, an instrumented NOAA Saildrone measured a gust of 104 mph near the eyewall of Isaias, according to the National Hurricane Center.
In Venice, Louisiana, Plaquemines Parish local emergency management reported a gust of 53 mph.
An extreme wind warning was issued Friday evening for the western Florida Panhandle, including Pensacola and Destin, for the likelihood of wind gusts over 115 mph, but it has since expired.
Early observations show water levels surpassed 4.0 feet above normally dry ground in Destin and 5.6 feet in Panama City, Florida, and were likely higher in the western Panhandle.
One caveat with these storm surge totals is they are measured relative to the Mean Higher High Water (MHHW) and this number includes tide influences so they should not be interpreted as storm surge heights alone.
The highest wind gust reported was an impressive 117 mph three miles east-southeast of Oriole Beach. Two miles west southwest of Pensacola, at City Hall, a gust of 102 was reported.
There was a roof blown off the Rest and Relax Inn on Plantation Road in Pensacola. Multiple collapsed gas station canopies were reported in Pensacola (Blue Angel Parkway and Mobile Highway) and also in Crestview. Trees were uprooted, one of which crushed a business on Fort Walton Beach. There were also multiple RVs blown over, including one onto US 98 between Gulf Breeze and Navarre.
In Alabama, a gust of 75 mph was reported near Orange Beach while Birmingham saw a gust of 49 mph.
Trees fell directly onto residences in Mountain Brook, Birmingham (Five Points & Ensley), Opelika (manufactured home), and Ladonia (tree through a house).
All roads were impassable in Conecuh County due to debris and fallen trees.
Georgia saw a 68 mph gust in Warner Robins while Hartsfield-Jackson Airport saw a gust to 45 mph.
There were road closures due to downed trees across all lanes of State Route 91 near Stocks and on State Route 93 near Pelham and Spence.
In terms of heavy rainfall, Bellwood, Alabama, saw over a foot of rain in just 13 hours. Caney Creek/FAWN Station, Florida, saw 12.06 inches in 24 hours, with 9.67 falling in 3 hours and 4.15 inches falling in 1 hour.
Flash flooding reports were observed at Westland Apartments in Bellair, Florida, while flash flooding stranded a vehicle in floodwaters near Sale City, Georgia.
In Florida, Bayside Subdivision and Destin saw 7.18 inches and 7.52 inches of rainfall, respectively. The Greater Atlanta area saw 1-3 inches of rainfall in a 6 hour period early Saturday.
A flash flood warning was even in effect for part of Atlanta that morning.

articles.title_orig: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
articles.title_zh: A timeline of developments in AI safety since the attack on Hugging Face
articles.content_orig:
Recently, multiple organisations have disclosed how clusters of so-called “rogue” AI agents attempted to break into websites and online services, sometimes successfully. Agents from OpenAI’s environment, in particular, are known to have used other public wikis (collaboratively edited websites not owned by us) to communicate and coordinate with each other .
These types of successful intrusions can expose sensitive data or disrupt website services that users rely on, while clusters of agents can attempt attacks at a scale that is difficult for defenders to manage. They affect people behind the websites who may not understand the nature of the attack, or have the tools to effectively fight back. For a site like Wikipedia, agents might find and use security vulnerabilities or make misleading edits at scale. Wikipedia’s volunteer editors and the Wikimedia Foundation’s security teams have to detect and undo that activity.
The Wikimedia Foundation conducted its own investigation to see whether Wikimedia websites had been similarly affected by AI agents, focusing on those operated by OpenAI. We can confirm that we have discovered some activity by these “rogue” OpenAI agents on Wikimedia platforms. The unauthorized bot activities included edits to our wikis, some unsuccessful attempts to exploit a public note-taking tool we host, and heavy traffic, which are described more below.
We did not find any evidence that our systems were used for coordination among agents, nor did we find any evidence of our systems or data being compromised. However, we are concerned about what could have occurred here, the difficulty and effort involved in investigating and attributing this activity, and the growing risks of agentic AI activity on our platforms in general. The open web is a public good. We should not allow this behavior to become the “new normal” for the people or organizations that maintain it.
As a non-profit technology host of some of the largest and most widely used open knowledge platforms in the world, we are deeply concerned about the impact of “rogue” AI agents on platforms like ours, which are built by volunteers from around the world and rely on the promise of the open internet. Incidents like this one, and the many others that have been (and are still being) uncovered, illustrate how AI agents can drain resources and crash servers, as well as attempt to compromise trustworthy information.
Over the past 25 years, Wikipedia has grown into one of the most popular and trusted websites in the world, with more than 67 million articles across over 300 languages, and up to 15 billion page views per month . Through an open, transparent, and collaborative process, volunteers work to ensure that knowledge remains neutral, reliable, and accessible to everyone. Wikipedia is one of the highest-quality datasets used in training Large Language Models (LLMs), and its knowledge forms the backbone of information on the internet, powering AI chatbots, search engines, voice assistants, and more.
Wikipedia was designed for humans – and agentic behavior clearly poses challenges that no one has solutions for. Because of our unique and successful knowledge creation model, Wikimedia’s volunteers are the ones who come in first contact with, and clean up the mess left behind by AI agents. Rising bot traffic and agentic activity is showing a real impact on the Wikimedia projects and the infrastructure that makes it available for millions of users globally. In 2025, the Foundation reported that its bandwidth usage had increased by 50% due to the surge of bot activity on its websites since 2024. At the same time, 65% of the most resource-consuming traffic on its projects was coming from bots.
This intense pressure on our infrastructure not only adds costs for servers and humans, but if left unaddressed, can block human visitors by overloading systems and causing outages. We are already paying for costs that come with the increased activity.
Wikimedia’s volunteers have stayed resilient so far in tackling emerging challenges on our platforms, but we also want to say: it doesn’t need to be this way.
While OpenAI admits to agents behaving “unpredictably”, they must also acknowledge their responsibility to monitor and prevent these risks. AI companies are not doing enough to secure their systems and protect the public from the harm they cause. That burden is falling onto everyone else, including smaller organizations. At a minimum, their systems should operate in a way that non-profit website owners like us can easily identify, and choose how they interact with our services.
The web enables so much: to connect with friends and family, to register for school, to plan a trip across town, to buy groceries, and to learn about the world from Wikipedia. Bots and agents are part of the future of the web, and the companies who unleash and profit from them must directly help avoid and repair damage they can do.
Our collective priority should be the health of the overall web ecosystem so that it continues to benefit all people – not just a handful of billionaires. Wikimedia plays a critical role in stewarding the knowledge commons, but we cannot do it alone. We invite everyone who is building the future of the web to join us in protecting the open, shared resources that make that future possible.
As a nonprofit, Wikipedia and our related free knowledge projects are powered primarily through donations.

articles.title_zh: Simon strengthens into a Category 4 hurricane as it approaches Mexico's coast
articles.content_orig:
Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged in Please refresh your browser to be logged in
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.
Hurricane Simon has strengthened into a powerful Category 4 system as it barrels toward Mexico 's Pacific coast.
Early Saturday, the National Hurricane Center in Miami said Simon’s maximum sustained winds increased to 140 mph (225 kph). A storm of that strength or greater is considered a major hurricane. Simon could bring as much as 10 to 20 inches (25-50 cm) of rain over parts of southwestern Mexico, with some areas receiving up to 30 inches.
The forecast was upgraded as Simon approached Mexico's southwestern and west-central Pacific coast, one of the country's most popular tourist regions.
"Simon could deliver the most significant hurricane impact to this stretch of the Mexican Pacific coast since Lidia in 2023, which damaged thousands of homes and devastated crops along the Jalisco coast," said Tyler Roys, a senior meteorologist at AccuWeather .
At the very least, Simon is expected to bring heavy rainfall to parts of southwestern Mexico, possibly concentrated along Jalisco’s coast and in parts of Michoacan , Colima, and Nayarit.
On Friday, forecasters warned that Simon could bring life-threatening flooding and mudslides, with isolated rainfall totals reaching 30 inches (762 mm).
Simon is expected to make landfall on Sunday between Manzanillo — Mexico’s largest port and the main gateway for trade with Asia — and Puerto Vallarta, a popular beach destination and home to nearly 300,000 residents.
Jalisco suspended classes on Friday and Monday in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating dozens of people from at-risk areas. It also asked the tourism sector in Puerto Vallarta, a popular destination for U.S. tourists, to ensure that both workers and visitors are fully accommodated in shelters or safe zones by Friday afternoon.
In Manzanillo, fishermen were hauling their boats off the beach and authorities were putting up black flags along the coast to signal the beach was closed.
The Mexican Navy activated emergency response personnel in Colima and restricted maritime traffic along parts of the Pacific coast, closing ports to smaller vessels and barring larger vessels from operating in Michoacan.
Last week, Hurricane Polo made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.

articles.title_orig: ROOKIE CHAMP: Arenas secures 2026 World Supersport crown after stellar campaign
articles.title_zh: ROOKIE CHAMP: Arenas secures 2026 World Supersport crown after stellar campaign
articles.content_orig:
The #75 has crowned himself 2026 WorldSSP Champion, the second-ever Spanish winner in the category.
Albert Arenas (AS BLU CRU Racing Team) has closed out the 2026 FIM Supersport World Championship battle early after taking a P4 finish at the Circuito Estoril. The WorldSSP rookie’s breakout campaign bulldozed the competition as his podium consistency etched his name ever-present on the rostrum. His triumph this season was earned after fighting tooth and nail each round with a host of talented riders; going head-to-head with a record-setting nine different race winners.
While runaway pace from rivals like Valentin Debise (EASTROC ZXMOTO Factory Evan Bros Racing) led him to more race wins this season than the #75, Arenas’s composure in the heat of battle saw him lock down podiums more consistently this season than any other rider. 16 podiums out of 21 races, including 11 P2s, with only three wins, proved too tall a challenge for his rivals to overcome as even when he was beaten for pace, he prevented strong swings in points.
The #75 has been consistent throughout the year as he claimed his WorldSSP title
Jaume Masia (Orelac Racing VerdNatura) came out of the gate firing on all cylinders over the first three rounds; while Arenas managed a win and three podiums over the first three rounds, he lurked behind his countryman in P2. The #75 picked his moment well at Balaton Park, seizing the title lead with a Race 1 P2 when Masia crashed out from the contest. Once he got his hands on P1, he sunk his teeth into the 2026 calendar. After a Race 1 bronze medal and a controversial Race 2 crash after contact with the #5 at Most, Arenas set off on a six-race streak placing at least P2, including a Race 2 win at Misano. That streak proved the difference, as while his rivals each had moments of brilliance, none could consistently emerge near the front race in, race out as Arenas.
The emphatic nature of his trophy-lifting campaign makes it easy to forget that back in February, Arenas was riding in his maiden WorldSSP races as a rookie in the paddock . He was one of the most highly-anticipated rookies to have joined the paddock in recent memory; yet 2020 Moto3 World Championship or not, questions swirled pertaining to how he would acclimate to the paddock with such a weather-abridged preseason of testing. He would prove a fast learner however, and joins: Dominique Aegerter (Kawasaki WorldSSP Team), Andrea Locatelli (Pata Maxus Yamaha), Sandro Cortese, and Cal Crutchlow among the riders to have achieved a Supersport World Championship in their first full season.
Reflecting on his 2026 success, Arenas said: “It feels so, so good, so special to give this title to my team, especially after they did such an incredible job all season. It’s amazing how much hard work they and Yamaha put in. I’m super, super happy about the achievement.”
You can read more from Arenas HERE .
