articles.title_orig: Winners and losers from Singapore GP 2026 F1 qualifying
articles.title_zh: Winners and losers from Singapore GP 2026 F1 qualifying
articles.content_orig:
A better evening for the championship leader’s upgraded car still wasn’t enough to get Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes into the Singapore Grand Prix pole fight , so it’s turning into a very good weekend for (one) Red Bull.
Here’s our full winners and losers rundown from qualifying.
Max Verstappen might just be one good start away from finally ending his Singapore hex and taking a grand prix victory on the one remaining circuit he has raced at regularly in F1 without winning.
He’s looked hooked up in the Red Bull this weekend as the 2026 car looks much more suited to the Marina Bay street circuit than its ground-effect predecessors ever did.
It wasn’t perfect. That Verstappen couldn’t improve on his final run left him vulnerable. But there’s no better place to start from if Verstappen is to make it two wins on the spin: although he’s clearly still not convinced by Red Bull’s startline troubles.
He was mugged off the line by George Russell in the sprint and Verstappen says there are “no excuses” for this given the sister Racing Bulls team is having good launches with the same software and hardware. - Scott Mitchell-Malm
A session that left the other Red Bull driver “pissed off” and wishing he’d stayed at home.
Isack Hadjar commended the work done by his Red Bull mechanics to get him out on track before a gearbox issue that “broke the fourth gear” and caused another abrupt end.
Hadjar was less than pleased after qualifying ended and went into somewhat of a spiral in his media session about his dislike for the current sprint format, the future sprint races and the “very disappointing” decision-making that led to more sprints being put on the calendar.
Part of the Red Bull driver’s frustration comes from having his excitement of getting over his handling issues ruined and the chance of points on Sunday now looking far from reality. Or, as he rather amusingly summed up: “I could’ve stayed back in Paris and it would’ve been the same [result.]” - Eden Hannigan
Kimi Antonelli’s gap to pole was cut from seven tenths to two tenths of a second from Friday to Saturday, a victory for the upgraded Mercedes.
Antonelli said: “We went completely opposite with the set-up [after the sprint race], and the car was in a happier place”.
The Race understands that the balance shift took the car away from generating too much oversteer and giving Antonelli a lack of confidence under braking.
Antonelli played around with differential settings during the sprint that dialled a lot of that oversteer out - leading to stronger pace later in the race - and that was followed by major set-up changes after the sprint, including raising the ride height and thus moving the aero balance back into a better window.
He thinks Mercedes should switch both its drivers to the new package for the next race at Austin so the team can keep experimenting to find the right window for its new upgrade.
Russell, a largely meaningless sixth in qualifying with a hefty engine penalty to serve for the race, wasn’t quite as glowing.
“It was positive to see Kimi more competitive today than yesterday, however, we weren't exactly lighting the timing screen on fire,” Russell said.
“As a team we’re still not satisfied with where we are with the new package. We recognise we need to make set-up adjustments to compensate for those changes. Maybe we can find a way to make it work, but right now we need more time.”
The upgraded Mercedes is still lagging behind the Red Bull and the Ferrari in Singapore at least, but it’s clearly made a step in the right direction. - Josh Suttill
A messy session that may leave Aston Martin even worse off than the initial qualifying results suggest.
Fernando Alonso already suggested he may take a grid penalty for a turbo issue that progressively worsened throughout Saturday’s action, culminating in a loss of power and momentum on the exits of the corners and a Q1 exit.
A lockup and a little bit of traffic were the story on the other side of the garage, as Lance Stroll surmised that the main Aston Martin issue comes from the bumpy nature of the Marina Bay circuit not working for its current package.
Given the track conditions are unlikely to change overnight, and the low grid positions could get even lower, the reality is a far cry from the pre-event aspirations of another potential points haul. - EH
After a bruising sprint where he faded badly with front tyre wear, this was Charles Leclerc at his best - dancing through discomfort to pull a very good qualifying lap out from nowhere.
He lagged badly behind Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton in Q1 and Q2, struggling with the car pulling to one side under braking, but with more “commitment” he turned the tables in Q3 and even got surprisingly close to pole.
Leclerc suggested he still wasn’t entirely happy with the car so, even beyond a front-row start typically being a good qualifying result, this worked out very well. - SMM
Context is critical for establishing why Hamilton ultimately lost out in qualifying.
Third on the grid is fine, especially when the gaps were so small. But it could have been so much more.
Leclerc said there was more in the Ferrari and Hamilton was the evidence. His theoretical best lap in Q3 was quicker than Verstappen’s, so if he had pieced together the sectors, he would be first. Plain and simple.
Hamilton had been delighted with his runs through Q1 and Q2 so to have that final outcome, after a Q3 in which he said neither lap was any good, is a loss. - SMM
Eight places down on Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly was more like the Franco Colapinto of old, rather than the driver who has been on terms with Gasly for much of the second half of the season.
Colapinto ended up in the wall in Q2 at Turn 17 but even before then he wasn’t looking likely to join Gasly in Q3.
“It's very strange,” Colapinto said of his 16th place. “Before the wall, I was already a lot slower than my Q1 lap, which normally you would improve a lot.
“So, I don't know, very strange, I had no rear grip the last lap. It was extremely poor, it was the worst balance I've had in the weekend.
“So, I don't know, a bit lost, to be honest, because Q1 felt quite easy to do the lap and it was coming not too bad, but then it was very, very poor.” - JS
For the third consecutive grand prix qualifying session, Gasly won F1’s midfield battle, beating both Racing Bulls in Q3.
Gasly called it “one of my best Q3s of the year” in a season he took pole at Monza, as he was thrilled with his execution on a sprint weekend.
He’s just hoping his Q3 appearance will translate into points, unlike in Azerbaijan and Malaysia.
“I must say the last few weekends, I think we have done four Q3s [including Singapore sprint] in the last four quali, but somehow we haven't scored that much because it's always gone wrong for whatever reason,” Gasly said.
“So as much as I would like a bit of chaos tomorrow, [it’s] hopefully not involving us another time, and hopefully we can translate this good quali into points.” - JS
Alex Albon was half a second slower than Williams team-mate Carlos Sainz in Q1 despite being “relatively happy with my lap”.
The data suggests the majority of that loss seems to come with the way Albon approached the tricky Turn 13 left-hander.
Team boss James Vowles said Albon “wasn’t as comfortable in the car” after Williams made repairs following the sprint, in which he shunted into the back of Gabriel Bortoleto’s Audi at the safety car restart.
Sainz’s Q2 was also compromised as Williams’s systems indicated he’d taken the chequered flag when he actually hadn’t - so he abandoned his lap and with it any chance of beating the Haas drivers.
“We will have a look overnight and see what changes we need to do so both drivers can come back stronger tomorrow,” Vowles said. - JS

articles.title_orig: Man dies after jumping into tiger enclosure at Yorkshire zoo
articles.title_zh: Man dies after jumping into tiger enclosure at Yorkshire zoo
articles.content_orig:
Police say man was pronounced dead at the scene after being attacked by tiger
A man has died after being attacked by a tiger after jumping into its enclosure at a zoo in Yorkshire , police have said.
Yorkshire Wildlife Park was evacuated shortly after the incident and the site will remain closed on Sunday.
South Yorkshire police said that at 1.35pm it received reports of an individual entering the enclosure at the zoo near Doncaster .
The force said the attack “resulted in serious injury”.
The statement added: “Emergency services attended and sadly, despite the best efforts of medical personnel, the man was pronounced dead at the scene.
“The man’s family is aware and is being supported by specialist officers. Our thoughts are with them at this distressing time.
“Regarding rumours surrounding the condition of the tiger, the animal was uninjured and remained in the enclosure following the incident and there is no wider risk to the public.”
The force earlier said: “We are aware of videos circulating online and we would encourage people not to share this distressing footage.”
Yorkshire Wildlife Park said a “serious incident” occurred inside the enclosure.
It said in a statement: “Our emergency response procedures were immediately activated, and emergency services are currently attending the scene.
after newsletter promotion
“We are working closely with the authorities to ascertain exactly what happened.” It added that the “safety and wellbeing of visitors, staff and animals remain our highest priority”.
Footage shared on social media appeared to show a man wearing a black jumper sitting on the ground of the enclosure and being attacked by a tiger.
A Yorkshire ambulance service spokesperson said it sent a number of resources to the scene including two ambulances, Yorkshire air ambulance and a doctor.

LITTLE COTTONWOOD CANYON, Oct. 10, 2026 (Gephardt Daily) — Salt Lake County Search and Rescue crews were dispatched to a Little Cottonwood Canyon area near China Wall Friday after a hiker fell while navigating a boulder field.
The fall was only about 10 feet, but left the hiker with a serious lower leg injury, and unable to stand or get back to the road.
SAR was dispatched to the scene at about 3:26 p.m. Friday. Unified Fire Authority was first on scene, and provided medical assistance to stabilized the patient’s knee.
An initial SAR team was dispatched with a litter and assisted UFA in packaging the patient for extraction.
Meanwhile, a second team was sent to assess the terrain and plan an exit route. Two additional teams followed to provide support for the ensuing carry-out.

SAR and UFA worked together to carry the patient across the boulder field, down the trail, through the creek, and back to the road.

There, a family member was waiting to drive them to the hospital for further evaluation.

articles.title_orig: Texas Rare Earths Could Challenge China And Bring Billions To Schools
articles.title_zh: Texas Rare Earths Could Challenge China And Bring Billions To Schools
articles.content_orig:
Texas could turn a West Texas rare earth deposit into a major source of school funding while reducing America’s reliance on China for critical minerals, Texas Land Commissioner Dawn Buckingham (R) said on Let’s Talk Local .
Round Top Mountain in Hudspeth County sits on state-owned land. Its development could connect two priorities Buckingham outlined in her interview with host Sarah Zubiate Bennett: securing essential materials at home and putting Texas resources to work for public education.
China accounted for 91% of global refining output for magnet rare earths in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency. That figure concerns processing, rather than ownership of all rare earth deposits.
“Well, your cell phones need rare earth minerals to work and jets require tons of them to fly,” Buckingham said in the interview.
Buckingham described domestic production as a national security priority and said she pushed prospective developers to compete rather than take the minerals to China for processing.
USA Rare Earth targets late 2028 for commercial production at Round Top. The company identifies processing facilities in Colorado and its magnet manufacturing facility in Stillwater, Oklahoma.
Bonus payments and royalties from the state’s Round Top lease go to the Permanent School Fund, which supports K-12 public education, according to the General Land Office.
“We think it’ll be tens of billions of dollars,” Buckingham said when asked about potential school-fund revenue. She also estimated the deposit could supply minerals for about 100 years.
As previously reported by The Dallas Express, Buckingham has linked revenue from state resources to public school funding and the burden on property owners.
The conversation also explores why she wants Texas to retain its land and how development could reshape the surrounding community.
Watch here for Buckingham’s explanation of the Round Top opportunity and what it could mean for Texas schools and American independence from China.

articles.title_orig: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
articles.title_zh: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
articles.content_orig:
President Mahmoud Abbas postponed what would have been the first Palestinian elections in nearly 20 years, issuing a decree on Friday to further delay voting for the Palestinian Legislative Council almost another year.
Rather than take place as scheduled next month, the decree pushes the elections back to Sept. 11, 2027, according to WAFA, the official Palestinian news agency. Presidential elections, which have not taken place for more than two decades, are scheduled for the same day.
The postponement leaves entrenched Palestinian leaders unchallenged and threatens to further erode the Palestinian Authority's credibility among ordinary Palestinians and donor countries who fund it.
The internationally backed body is dominated by Abbas' party, Fatah, and has administered semiautonomous parts of the Israeli-occupied West Bank since agreements reached in the 1990s. It has grown increasingly unpopular throughout Abbas' presidency. Many Palestinians view it as corrupt and criticize its security cooperation with Israel.
The decree came after a committee of top Palestinian officials met Saturday morning to discuss postponing the vote. The Palestine Liberation Organization's Executive Committee, which Abbas heads, said in a statement that conditions in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and the Gaza Strip were not conducive to holding elections, noting that Israel had not allowed election materials or international observers to enter Gaza.
The move was expected after Palestinian factions across the political spectrum met in Cairo for discussions on delaying the vote, Islamic Jihad deputy secretary-general Mohammed al-Hindi told The Associated Press earlier this week.
Palestinians have not held a legislative election since 2006, when Hamas won a majority of seats. Israel and Western countries then boycotted its government, fueling months of unrest that led to the Hamas takeover of Gaza the following year. Power has been divided between Gaza and the West Bank in the two decades since, with Hamas in control of Gaza and Abbas' Palestinian Authority in power in the West Bank.
The West Bank has grown increasingly violent in recent years as Israel has expanded settlements and outposts. Settler attacks on Palestinians and Israeli army raids on cities under the authority's control are both regularly reported.
Though the U.S.-brokered ceasefire plan reached last year outlined a future role for the authority, its immediate role was left mostly undefined as Hamas has continued to govern and the technocrats under the Board of Peace remain in Cairo awaiting permission to enter Gaza to transition power.
Before the postponement, leading factions had not registered slates to contest the election. But behind the scenes, veteran officials had been in talks to join forces and take aim at Abbas. An unlikely alliance had emerged between Hamas, Islamic Jihad and a bloc led by former Fatah security chief Mohammed Dahlan. Dahlan had previously been driven from Gaza by Hamas and was exiled in 2010 after a falling-out with Abbas.
"Abbas is terrified by the electoral alliance bringing our faction together with opposition factions and forces within Fatah that reject his leadership," Dimitri Dilliani, a spokesperson for Dahlan's faction, said in a statement.
Abbas has served as president since 2005 and delayed several presidential and legislative elections throughout his tenure.

"It's one of the most devastating things that's happened to our family," he said. "And their family is just … as you can imagine, it's the worst thing that could ever happen to a family."

He reportedly checked into the Resolutions Living facility on Sept. 19.
Clooney is a longtime friend of the Gerber family and co-founded Casamigos Tequila with Rande. He was reportedly referred to as "Uncle George" by the Gerber children.
In the days following Presley's death, the actor and his wife, Amal Clooney, were spotted stepping out of their car as they arrived at Kaia Gerber's home in Los Angeles.

articles.title_orig: New Google TV Streamer: Big Upgrades are Coming
articles.title_zh: New Google TV Streamer: Big Upgrades are Coming
articles.content_orig:
The Google TV Streamer is now well over 2 years old , if you can believe that. The streaming media box with its sleek pill-shaped design, was once the easiest recommendation in the business for someone looking to upgrade their not-that-smart smart TV.
But because we’ve reached the 2-year mark and Google handed the streamer a substantial price increase without any upgrades, there may be other options to explore before settling on Google’s box. You could also wait for a new model, which is reportedly in the works and has a handful of decent upgrades.
According to a report from 9to5Google , Google is working on the next-generation Google TV Streamer with several key improvements.
For one, the box will remain with a similar design, but Google is going to add microphones to it and also presence sensing. This should allow you to talk to it like a Google Home unit, but the presence sensing could aid in noticing your arrival in a room to showcase something like a Google Photos screensaver.
The new Google TV Streamer will reportedly gain a faster processor too, as well as more storage than the original, which only has 32GB.
Finally, we should see a new remote that will be similar yet include a couple of new shortcut buttons. The mini remote from the original Chromecast with Google TV was clearly not everyone’s favorite. While I’m not asking for a large remote, a few extra buttons and some additional length can go a long way in in-hand feel improvement.
What will the new Google TV Streamer cost and when might it launch? The report isn’t sure. That said, we do have some history to look at.
The Chromecast with Google TV 4K launched in 2020 . Google then gave us the HD version in 2022 before the Google TV Streamer hit store shelves in 2024. Google was on a 2-year TV product release cadence, but there are no signs of a new model launching before the end of 2026. I’d guess that 2027 could be the earliest we’ll see an updated Google TV Streamer.
Droid Life was started in 2009 and I can't believe we're still here. I've written over 20,000 stories on Android, reviewed thousands of devices, and still find some passion in a dying world of AI.

articles.title_orig: Unnerved Panamanians sleep in streets as aftershocks rattle quake-hit towns
articles.title_zh: Unnerved Panamanians sleep in streets as aftershocks rattle quake-hit towns
articles.content_orig:
A major earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 7.7 has struck southern Panama, according to the US Geological Survey.
Several people have suffered minor injuries but so far there are no reports of fatalities or missing persons, officials said. Various homes, roads, hotels, government buildings, businesses and churches have sustained structural damage, according to the civil protection system.
The USGS had said some casualties were possible and extensive damage was probable. The earthquake was followed by 147 aftershocks, director of the Emergency Operations Center René García told CNN. Some of those aftershocks reached magnitudes of 6.1 or 6.6.
García said authorities are waiting for the tremors to subside before conducting structural inspections of damaged buildings. The most significant damage has been reported in Coclé province on the nation’s southern coast, although some has also been seen in the capital, Panama City.
Footage verified by CNN shows several damaged buildings in Penonome, some 70 miles from the epicenter. One video shows a church with a partially collapsed steeple and another building with a crumbled facade.
In the popular resort town Playa Venao, a multi-story building collapsed and crushed several cars beneath it.
Along the Panama Canal, the Centennial Bridge’s suspension cables were seen shaking as vehicles drove through.
The canal authority said operations were continuing as normal and that staff were inspecting facilities for damage.
Panama City’s public transit system has suspended service on two metro lines and evacuated passengers from some stations.
Scores of residents gathered in the streets of the capital after rushing out of their buildings in a panic.
“I am on the ninth floor here and yes it was felt strongly,” Panama City resident Kevin Cortez told Reuters.
“Everything was moving: the lamp, the chair, the table,” another resident said. “I decided to stay and wait because I knew running down the stairs was a problem. So I stayed waiting for it to pass. I had no other option. Yes, we felt it was quite prolonged. People running, shouting; not everyone takes it the same way, but well, here we are, downstairs.”
The Education Ministry has canceled classes nationwide for the rest of the day.
Panama’s main international airport was temporarily closed as a precaution and flights were diverted to other airports before operations resumed later in the day, the civil aviation authority said.
The water and sewage institute has reported interruptions at several water treatment plants due to power outages caused by the quake.
Panama’s President José Raúl Mulino has called for calm and instructed the minister of government to provide information on the earthquake’s effects. He has also mobilized resources to those affected.
Mulino visited an affected hospital in Penonome, where several patients were evacuated and have had to receive treatment outdoors.
Earlier, the US Tsunami Warning System warned of possible tsunami waves along some coasts, before saying there was no longer a threat.
This is just the latest powerful earthquake to have struck Latin America this year. Over the summer, Venezuela was hit by two powerful earthquakes that killed more than 6,400 people, while Colombia suffered a tremor that left around 300 dead.
The leaders of both countries have offered to help Panama’s government as it responds to the disaster.
CNN’s Mauricio Torres contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Joel Oxley Goes Out on ’TOP
articles.title_zh: Joel Oxley Goes Out on ’TOP
articles.content_orig:
Update your browser to view this website correctly. Update my browser now
Home › News and Business › News Makers
Hubbard Radio’s WTOP(FM) has been one of the top revenue-generating stations in the United States for more than a decade, according to BIA estimates. Although it is in Nielsen Market No. 8, it regularly beats out stations in the larger markets to pull off that feat.
WTOP’s over-the-air revenue in 2023, the most recent for which BIA published estimates, was $66.3 million. WTOP led the BIA list 13 times over the previous 14 years. It also pulls in consistently high ratings.
That remarkable streak occurred under the leadership of Joel Oxley, president/GM of WTOP, WFED(AM), the Federal News Network and the 2060 Digital Washington platform.
Oxley, who is about to retire, has been named to receive the 2026 NAB National Radio Award from the National Association of Broadcasters .
We asked him about the uniqueness of the Washington market, changes in newsroom workflows and his secret to generating revenue. Text has been edited for length and clarity.
Radio World: Are you optimistic about the radio broadcast business model going forward?
Joel Oxley: Yes, I think it can still work, but I think you’ve got to have great products, and you must have products that connect to people. You’ve also got to understand that radio is great distribution still. But you’ve got to be playing in all the platforms. As long as you do that, radio can be still a great part of the business.
But it’s not the 1990s anymore. You’ve got to be looking at the business model differently. You can’t be sitting around waiting for agency avails — I mean it’s great when you get agency avails, we love agencies when they call us and give us a bit of business. [But] you have to be incredibly proactive and make sure that you’re getting out and figuring out what you can do to help solve your clients’ needs.
Find solutions. It could be digital. It might not be over the air radio every time.
RW: Does AM have a future as the margins continue to shrink?
Oxley: That’s really going to be market-dependent, signal-dependent. It’s getting harder. I don’t think anybody would tell you that it’s an easy business. We have found some good uses for our AMs, and I think others can too.
Especially when AMs are paired with translators, especially smaller markets, they make a whole hell of a lot of sense.
We’ve experimented with AM digital. There are ways to make AM sound better. There can still be a place for it. But I’m not going to tell you that it’s an easy business.
RW: What makes the Washington radio market unique?
Oxley: I tell people: It’s always a good thing to be in the all-news business in the news capital of the world.
The market has really grown, too. It wasn’t that long ago, honestly, that it was a 2-million-person market. Now it’s over 6 million. If you throw in Baltimore, it’s like 9.
Also the growth of the federal government has meant a lot more jobs have come here. All kinds of government contractors. That’s what makes us unique.
Unlike most markets, there’s also a lot of political influence advertising here, and that’s a great advertising category for us. There’s more issue money spent here than anywhere.
Advocacy money used to be really big for us, but it’s a smaller part of what we do now.
However, the government contracting side has grown a ton, and we see that as an area that’s going to continue to grow.
RW: Many radio companies are downsizing their physical footprint. You opened a large new facility seven years ago. Do you still need that much space now?
Oxley: No, we don’t. The reality is a lot more people work remotely now.
The tools are so much better. Our reporters, a lot of them do amazing things with just an iPhone with audio and video.
Our remote work has increased significantly. The workflows have changed. Salespeople can work from anywhere. Docking stations and good connectivity means that you can do your job from all over the place with a laptop, let alone your phone.
So if I had it to do over again, we wouldn’t need anywhere near as much space as we have.
RW: How is AI changing how work gets done in the WTOP newsroom?
Oxley: Lots of ways. But we’re being trying to be very careful and thoughtful about it. Certainly, being in the news business, we cannot afford mistakes. We can’t afford misinformation.
We insist that everything that we do has a pair of human eyes on it, and that people are reading it through, proofreading, fact-checking. We’ve got to make sure things are right. If you lose your credibility, you’ve lost.
RW: Do you worry about the future of all-news radio given the massive amount of instantly available information that Americans now have right on their phone?
Oxley: Sure. You’ve got to always be concerned about that. But we’re on the phone, too, for people to consume our products.
RW: There is great pressure to compete with digital platforms. You’ve gone through the digital transition. How do you choose which ones are successful without diluting the original value of the radio broadcast business?
Oxley: It’s a point a lot of people miss. It’s great to go into all kinds of different platforms and all kinds of different things, but you got to make sure you get ROI. You’ve got to make sure that there is a business plan. You can’t just go into it without making sure that you’re also supporting that with advertising.
I think that’s a missing piece for a lot of folks. They go into it and they’re getting tons of hits or tons of views, but they don’t do much because you can’t monetize.
RW: The Federal News Network airs on WFED(AM), which isn’t a highly rated station. Why is the network successful?
Oxley: So it’s not a ratings play. It’s about reaching the right people. It’s reaching government decisionmakers. CIOs for example, really high up in the government levels.
And while we really don’t see that necessarily in the ratings, we do see it in our streaming numbers and our podcast numbers, where we see the number of people who are consuming that product. It goes pretty deep.
These are things that really matter to the upper levels of government, and we know that we’re getting pretty good numbers there. But it’s a niche play for sure.
Sometimes it’s about getting the right thousand people. Sometimes about getting the right six people. Sometimes it’s about getting the right two people. So it’s a different play than broadcast in a sense, but it’s been going really well for us.
RW: You’ve supported the work done by Dave Kolesar with AM HD Radio at WSHE Frederick, Md., formerly WWFD. It’s a full digital-only station. What does the future look like for full-time digital AM and for that station specifically?
Oxley: I’ll tell you, it sounds so much better. I think that it’s something that if you can find the right format, it’s going to be a much better play than trying to just go with traditional AM. I don’t know that it’s necessarily been proven yet, that somebody can make a business out of that.
I still think it’s a viable way to go because it does make me forget that I’m on AM. It’s like I’m listening to FM.
RW: You play music but no commercials on that station. How long can that go on for?
Oxley: It’s more of a public service play right now. It’s more experimental. No, it’s not making a profit.

Oxley: I don’t think it is what anybody expected it to be. I think it also came out late. And adoption has not been maybe as strong as people like. But I’m not sure that everybody knows how to use it, so it’s still a bit of an uphill battle.

articles.title_orig: JD Vance says he won't watch livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter
articles.title_zh: JD Vance says he won't watch livestream execution of Fort Hood shooter
articles.content_orig:
Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s announcement that the execution of the convicted Fort Hood mass shooter would be shown in public caught people across the Pentagon and the Army off guard, three sources familiar with the matter told CNN.
Hegseth made the announcement in an interview Wednesday with far-right podcaster Jack Posobiec aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, where he welcomed the crew home from their monthslong deployment to the Middle East.
“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public, because people need to understand that there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said during the interview.
That comment was the first time many in the Army and Pentagon heard about the idea of a firing squad’s execution of Nidal Hasan in Texas being made public, and there were immediately questions about what “public” would mean. There are Army regulations about who can watch a military execution, including family of the prisoner and of the victims, media representatives and a chaplain.
But it was decided by Hegseth, acting Army Secretary Adam Telle, and Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell and his staff that “public” would mean it would be livestreamed, one source familiar said. The Pentagon then confirmed as much to the media, saying in a statement, “The Secretary is correct. It will be livestreamed. Details will follow.”
Hegseth wants America to watch a firing squad execution. It’s drawing backlash
The Army referred questions to the Pentagon, and a Pentagon spokesperson said they had nothing to add beyond Thursday’s confirmation that it would be livestreamed.
The idea has shocked many service members and veterans and provoked a bipartisan backlash . Vice President JD Vance cast doubt on Friday that the livestream could ultimately go forward, saying he didn’t know “if that’s actually going to happen,” but said if it was, “I’m not going to be watching it.”
“It takes away everything America stands for when we do public executions,” one Army officer with multiple deployments to the Middle East told CNN. “The generational harm caused by allowing troops in uniform to stand in front of a man in a wheelchair and watch him get shot to death is irreparable.”
President Donald Trump welcomed the idea of a firing squad execution throughout the week but on Saturday said he hasn’t decided whether to livestream it.
“We’re giving a man the death penalty who killed 14 soldiers a couple of years ago. Death penalty through firing squad — and he deserves it,” the president said to applause during a White House event Friday honoring Christopher Columbus.
Trump told reporters Saturday, “I’ll make a decision, ultimately. I know what the military would like to do, but we’ll make a decision.”
Many of the details around the livestream have yet to be finalized, and multiple sources told CNN that officials have been working to find answers since it was announced. A second source familiar told CNN that great care is being taken to determine which soldiers would fire on Hasan, taking into consideration the potential psychological impacts of doing so. A specific unit has been selected to carry out the execution, the source said.
Showing the execution on a livestream presents more challenges, the source said, including any effort to obscure from the public the identities of the soldiers involved. It’s also unclear where and if the execution will be streamed beyond the Pentagon’s own website. Broadcasters and social media platforms have strict restrictions on violent and disturbing content.
The first source familiar said there are still questions about whether soldiers can decline to participate, given that the military is moving forward with this as a legal order.
The second source familiar echoed the same, saying while many soldiers may have “taken a life in combat,” this is a very different situation.
“This is a situation where the guy has done a very bad thing and hurt a lot of people, years removed,” the second source said. “He’s going to be immobile and put up like a target.”
This story has been updated with additional details.

articles.title_orig: Vehicle driven by ICE agents in Texas hits and injures man, sheriff says
articles.title_zh: Vehicle driven by ICE agents in Texas hits and injures man, sheriff says
articles.content_orig:
A vehicle driven by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents hit and injured a man in the greater Houston area on Saturday, the Harris County Sheriff's Office said.
"The incident appears to have occurred while ICE authorities were conducting an enforcement action in the area," the sheriff's office said in a statement.
During a press conference, Major McConnell of the Harris County Sheriff's special investigation bureau said the sheriff's office was called to the scene around 7:20 a.m.
ICE agents were headed south in pursuit of a wanted suspect, McConnell said, and the suspect drove west in an eastbound lane. The suspect bailed out of his vehicle and went on foot, he said.
The driver and passenger fled and ICE agents attempted to capture them both, he said. While trying to capture the passenger, the ICE agent hit him with his vehicle.
The victim was taken to a local hospital. McConnell said it appears the man has a broken leg, but no further details were given on the man's condition.
McConnell said the victim is a 48-year-old male and is currently in the custody of ICE at the hospital.
CBS News reached out to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security for more information.

articles.title_orig: Mixed Teams Preview: When Judo Becomes a Collective Force
articles.title_zh: Mixed Teams Preview: When Judo Becomes a Collective Force
articles.content_orig:
For a week, the focus has been on the individual, on each judoka and their chance to perform. On the final day, that focus shifts to the team, as the mixed team event takes centre stage. It is one of the most eagerly anticipated moments of the championships and it never fails to raise the volume in the arena. From the opening contests, groups of supporters will be on their feet, cheering for their teams.
The draw has been known for a week, giving delegations time to prepare and fine-tune the line-up of six judoka: three women and three men. For some nations, the choices are straightforward, with one athlete available in each category. Others must weigh up several factors, including how fresh their athletes are after a demanding week, as well as the tactical options available. Some judoka may compete in a higher weight category than they did for the individual event, for instance.
The aim is to build the most balanced and united team, one capable of upsetting the predictions. In this event, team spirit and momentum can make all the difference. Georgia proved that in 2025, when it became the first nation to deny Japan the mixed team world title.
Will the story be different this year? Based on the individual results, Japan is the clear favourite. Yet success on paper does not guarantee that everything will come together on the day. Teams with fewer individual titles can find the energy and cohesion to unsettle the strongest nations. We have seen it many times, including at the Olympic Games: France beat Japan in both editions of the Olympic mixed team event, with their victory at Paris 2024 providing one of the most memorable moments of the Games.
Back in Baku, the host nation will be among those looking to make the most of home support. Azerbaijan and Austria, along with Russia and the United Arab Emirates, will begin in the preliminary round, with those results shaping the next stage of the draw.
Elsewhere, Brazil will be looking to put a quieter individual week behind them when they face China. The winners will meet either Cuba or Türkiye. Japan will be a formidable presence in thei section and could meet the winner of a Mongolia-Kyrgyzstan match, provided they come through their earlier challenge.
The other half of the draw also promises compelling contests. Defending champions Georgia will face Italy, whose athletes have impressed throughout the week. The winners will go on to meet either Uzbekistan or Germany.
The lower part of the draw brings together several strong teams, including Korea, Russia, Kazakhstan and France. The United Arab Emirates will also be in the mix, buoyed by Yelyzaveta Lytvynenko, the country’s first-ever world champion.
It is difficult to look too far ahead. Team line-ups are not yet confirmed,m and substitutions can still change the picture. What is certain is that, from 9am local time, the National Gymnastics Arena will be alive with noise. In the mixed team event, every point belongs to the team and every cheer can help carry them forward.

articles.title_orig: Two dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle
articles.title_zh: Two dead as Isaias weakens to post-tropical cyclone after striking Florida panhandle
articles.content_orig:
Some of deaths came from falling trees as nearly a million people are without power and rain and flooding remain a concern
Hurricane Isaias latest updates – live
At least four people were reported dead on Saturday amid Isaias after it made landfall late on Friday on Florida’s panhandle as a category 2 hurricane, according to authorities.
The storm also took down trees, knocked out electricity for hundreds of thousands and flooded highways – but as Saturday evening approached, the region was reopening.
Two of the deaths reported during Isaias occurred in Escambia county, Florida , and two others were reported in Alabama , as the storm moved inland, local officials said. Of those deaths, one each occurred in Escambia and Birmingham, Alabama, when trees fell on homes.
Another person whose death was linked to Isaias was found in a closed garage with a running generator in Escambia county. Four members of that person’s family have been transported to the hospital with carbon monoxide poisoning, the Escambia sheriff’s office said.
“Don’t run any generators inside your home, it can be very, very hazardous,” Florida governor Ron DeSantis said in a press conference.
In Alabama , governor Kay Ivey said Isaias – predicted to dissipate on Sunday – “cannot clear fast enough”.
Meanwhile, though it had weakened on Saturday to a post-tropical cyclone, Isaias still posed flooding and tornado threats as it moved inland, forecasters and officials warned.
“Remember, there can still be flooding from rising rivers,” Jared W Perdue, the secretary of Florida’s state transportation department, said at a news conference. “I’m just going to remind all of you – please, if there’s standing water or flowing water on top of a road, please do not drive through it.
“It does not have to be that deep, and it can wash away your car, it can wash away a human, it can become very dangerous very quickly.”
More than 679,000 customers were without power across Florida, Alabama and Georgia on Saturday afternoon as those in the path of the storm began the cleanup process, according to PowerOutage .us . Though still high, the number of outages was down from more than 900,000 earlier on Saturday.
Storm surge and tropical storm warnings associated with Isaias by then had been discontinued, the National Hurricane Center (NHC) warned there would still likely be “considerable impacts” associated with Isaias across much of southern Alabama, Florida’s panhandle and south-western Georgia .
“Flash, urban and river flooding is possible across the region,” the NHC said in a Saturday-morning advisory, adding that there was a considerable potential for flash flooding and landslides across the southern Appalachians. “A risk for tornadoes will persist … through [Saturday] afternoon across parts of the eastern Florida panhandle, Georgia and the Carolinas.”
Isaias through Sunday is expected to produce rainfall amounts of 4-8in across southern Alabama, Florida’s panhandle and Big Bend regions, and south-west Georgia. Localized totals up to 15in are possible, particularly within rain bands across the Florida panhandle and Big Bend.
Across much of the remainder of the south-east US, rainfall amounts of 2-5in are expected, and localized higher amounts up to 10in are possible, especially across the southern Appalachians and coastal Carolinas.
Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday as a potent category 2 hurricane. It was an atypically late-forming first Atlantic hurricane of the season and lashed the US Gulf coast with heavy rain, fierce winds and life-threatening flooding.
Hurricane Milton ’s strike on Florida in October 2024 was the last time a hurricane hit the mainland US before Isaias.
The hurricane’s maximum sustained winds were 105mph (169km/h). That was intense enough to sound like “a train whistle”, Tim Mowry told the Associated Press after enduring the storm as his home in Pensacola, Florida.
after newsletter promotion
Mowry described losing power on Friday afternoon but said could rely on a generator. He said his son tried to drive to his home after his place about 15 minutes away lost power but had to turn around because downed trees and power lines blocked the road.
All things considered, Mowry said he was “really fortunate” with respect to how he fared during Isaias.
Ashley Weeks, a resident of Crestview, Florida, told the news station WEAR that a tree from her backyard fell on top of her house, damaging the the roof near her daughter’s bedroom and turning the ceiling into piles of debris.
It was “just scary – everything, my whole life is in the house”, Weeks said. “We heard a loud … like a bomb went off in the house. It was so loud. And I got up and [saw] the tree through the roof, and it was – freaking out.”
While the stronger El Niño seemed to limit the number of hurricanes in the Atlantic for the year so far, Isaias forming in October with maximum sustained winds of 105mph marked a stark contrast from historical trends.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) predicted a quiet year in terms of hurricanes at the beginning of a season that officially begins annually on 1 June. Noaa anticipated between three and six hurricanes, well below the average of seven. An August forecast from Noaa cut the expected number to between two and six.
Isais is one of the two latest-forming Atlantic hurricanes on record, tying a record set on 8 October 1905. Otherwise, the second-latest date for the first Atlantic hurricane was 11 September – in 2002 and 2013.
None of the eight previous named storms of the 2026 Atlantic season intensified above tropical storm status.
The Associated Press contributed reporting

articles.title_orig: Indian police crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in Delhi
articles.title_zh: Indian police crack down on 'Cockroach' protest in Delhi
articles.content_orig:
Here is our rolling coverage of developments from India on Saturday, October 10:
Videos released by opposition leaders show that several senior figures were detained in New Delhi on Saturday.
They include Arvind Kejriwal, leader of the Aam Aadmi Party and former chief minister of Delhi .
"It's official... we are living under an absolute dictatorship," Kejriwal wrote on X.
Mamata Banerjee, who lost power as West Bengal's chief minister earlier this year, was also detained.
Pinarayi Vijayan, a communist leader who headed the southern state of Kerala until May, was among those detained.
Rahul Gandhi, leader of India's opposition Congress party , called the crackdown an act of "cowardice" and described Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, right-wing, Hindu nationalist RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval as "the villains of this story" who were "slowly finding the space closing around them. We are closing that space."
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul Gandhi's sister and a Congress MP, wrote in a social media post: "India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Mr. Narendra Modi and Mr. Amit Shah."
Opposition parties and critics have warned that the electoral-roll revision exercise could strip millions of people of their voting rights and give an advantage to Prime Minister Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
The Election Commission of India has rejected allegations of wrongdoing, saying the "special intensive revision" aims to remove duplicate and ineligible voters.
The protests echo the CJP's mass mobilization in July, which forced the then education minister to resign over an examination scandal.
This time, demonstrators are demanding the resignation of election chief Gyanesh Kumar.
Tens of thousands of security personnel have been deployed and roads barricaded across New Delhi to prevent the latest Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) demonstration.
Police have detained thousands of protesters in a major crackdown. Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders were detained before disembarking from a flight in the capital.
Some protesters who turned back from Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site, have been waiting in different parts of central Delhi, determined to hold their ground.
The CJP has urged people who believe they or someone they know has been unlawfully detained to fill out an online form as soon as possible, saying it is collecting information to support affected volunteers and other individuals.
The protest targeted Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over voter list revisions that critics say favor Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling BJP.
If you're joining us now, here's a helpful reminder about why India's youth are rising up this time.
DW Hindi's Adarsh Sharma, who is on the ground in New Delhi, spoke to protesters as they faced a security crackdown.
He caught up with one protester who managed to avoid detention.
"We were running back and forth. When the police are moving forward, we go back. When they are withdrawing, we are moving forward," the protester told DW.
The protester described the heavy police presence as a "game of perception."
"Where you have 20 protesters and 10 media persons, there are 100 police personnel standing. It seems like a joke, what they are doing with taxpayers' money," the protester said.
Another protester, Jasmine, described how the morning unfolded for the demonstrators.
"We have been playing a game of cat and mouse with the police, trying to stop them from picking us up," she said.
"I don't think we have ever seen something like this happening. Protesting is a fundamental right… it's such a convoluted idea to take permission to protest… you are protesting against a government, will you ask permission from the same government? They are not going to give it," she said.
Ajinkya Shinde, who was handed the responsibility of leading the Cockroach Janta Party's protest following the detentions of its main leaders, has made his first statement — calling for a continued march to Jantar Mantar.
"We appeal to everyone to march towards Jantar Mantar! If Delhi Police tries to stop you, wherever they stop you will become your Jantar Mantar," he said in a video post made by the CJP on X.
Indian media outlets, including Scroll and Newslaundry, reported that their journalists had been detained by police while covering the 'Cockroach' party protest. The journalists were later released.
Newslaundry reported that police seized its reporters’ phones, while other reports said journalists were physically assaulted.
The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ), an independent nonprofit organization that promotes press freedom and defends journalists' rights worldwide, has called on Delhi Police to immediately release all detained journalists and media workers.
It has also urged police to return their equipment, investigate reports of physical abuse, and allow the press to cover the ongoing protests in New Delhi and the police response without interference.
In the 2026 World Press Freedom Index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF), India ranked 157th out of 180 countries, down six places from 2025. Press freedom groups have raised concerns about the use of criminal laws against journalists and the impact of such measures on independent journalism.
Detained Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke's grandmother is reported to have died on Saturday.
Indian media reports said that Dipke's paternal grandmother had been suffering from a prolonged illness and had been unwell in recent days. She died in her native village in Maharashtra, reports said.
News agency ANI, citing police sources, reported that the Delhi Police had informed Dipke of his grandmother's death. It was now up to the CJP leader to decide whether to continue his protest while under detention or travel back for the funeral rites.
Dipke was detained aboard his plane after it landed in New Delhi on Saturday morning, ahead of the protest. He was traveling from Mumbai.
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has indicated that it will press on with its protest despite its leaders and supporters being detained.
CJP's National Organization In-Charge Ajinkya Shinde will lead the protest at Jantar Mantar until Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in detention, the group said in a statement on X.
The CJP also shared a video of Dipke purportedly recorded on Friday night, anticipating a potential detention.
"If you are seeing this video, it means Ashutosh, Saurav and I have been arrested," Dipke says in the video.
"After us, Ajinkya will lead this movement," he says.
In a separate post, the CJP alleged that its three detained leaders had been taken to an undisclosed location, were being denied access to lawyers and had been cut off from "all contact with others."
The formal association of advocates at India's apex court called for urgent intervention by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant after several lawyers were detained by Delhi police.
This comes amid a reported crackdown on protesters attempting to reach the national capital, specifically central Delhi, to protest against India's chief election commissioner over alleged misconduct.
The arrested lawyers include those protesting outside the premises of the Supreme Court of India, as well as lawyers inside their chambers, legal news website, Bar and Bench, reported.
The Supreme Court Bar Association passed a resolution condemning the use of "excessive force against, and detention of, senior and young advocates, particularly women advocates, who were peacefully protesting in the Supreme Court area today."
The advocates' body expressed "grave concern" and requested the CJI to take action to ensure that the "whereabouts and safety of every detained advocate are ascertained."

articles.title_orig: Different voices, shared challenges: mental health in athletics | FEATURE
articles.title_zh: Different voices, shared challenges: mental health in athletics | FEATURE
articles.content_orig:
Mental health in athletics
It was a fleeting exchange at a press conference, but it touched on a much wider issue.
Speaking at the World Athletics Relays in Gaborone earlier this year, Zaynab Dosso and Elaine Thompson-Herah were both asked about the mental side of elite sport.
Italian sprinter Dosso was clear about the importance she places on it. “It’s very important to speak about mental health,” said the world indoor 60m champion. “You can train however many hours you want, but if your head doesn’t follow then you’re not going to get anywhere.
“Last September I started working with a psychologist. Every single athlete should take care of their mental health because it’s just as important as their physical health.”
The same question was then put to Thompson-Herah. “Coming back from injury has been challenging, mentally and physically,” said the five-time Olympic champion.
“But I’m a tough cookie. I’ve never been to therapy, I don’t believe in it. I’m my own therapy. I do believe in God, though. I also have a supportive team who believes in me, and I believe in myself.”
The contrast was striking. Both athletes acknowledged the mental challenges of elite sport, yet they had very different ideas about how to deal with them.
Across a sport spanning more than 200 countries, there are inevitably huge differences in the way mental health is understood, discussed and treated. Professional psychological support may be commonplace for some athletes. Others may turn first to family, friends, teammates or coaches. Elsewhere, stigma, lack of awareness or limited access to services can make the route to support far less straightforward.
US 800m runner Juliette Whittaker has spoken with remarkable openness about her own experience. During her time at Stanford University, Whittaker won two individual NCAA titles before qualifying for the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. Her results suggested a young athlete whose career was progressing almost perfectly.
Juliette Whittaker in action at the US Olympic Trials (© Getty Images)
The reality was very different. She later described it as the “hardest, saddest and loneliest” year of her life.
After winning her first NCAA title, the happiness had disappeared by the following day. After the second, it lasted less than an hour. Whittaker responded by setting herself another target, believing that perhaps reaching the Olympics would finally make her feel differently. It didn’t.
“I truly believed that if I ran well enough, achieved enough, proved myself enough, I would finally feel enough,” she said.
Instead, her sense of self-worth became increasingly tied to her performances. When running stopped providing the fulfilment she expected from it, she struggled to know where else to find it. After returning from Paris, her mental health deteriorated further. Feelings of emptiness became guilt and shame, and she stopped telling people how badly she was struggling.
In May 2025, Whittaker attempted to take her own life.
Friends found her and took her to hospital. She spent a week in a psychiatric unit and later attended group therapy three days a week, while also taking the longest break from running she had ever had.
Whittaker credits the people around her with playing a huge part in her recovery. “At a time when I had completely given up on myself, I had villages of people who refused to give up on me,” she said, speaking at Stanford’s GameFaces event earlier this year.
“One year ago, I was in a hospital bed with absolutely no desire to live,” she added. “Today I’m standing in front of you.”
Her experience also changed the way she viewed athletics. “Running is a huge part of my life,” she said. “But it is not all of me. It is not the source of my worth.”
After spending so long keeping her feelings to herself, she had learned another lesson: “Asking for help is one of the bravest things you can do.” But asking for help assumes an athlete recognises what is happening to them, feels able to talk about it and knows where to turn.
Research in recent years has examined some of those barriers in different parts of the world.
A 2025 paper on mental health among elite runners in Kenya highlighted the importance of cultural and socioeconomic context. Its authors pointed to issues including the availability, accessibility and affordability of mental-health services, and cautioned against assuming that approaches developed in wealthier countries can simply be transferred elsewhere.
A separate 2024 study involving 20 Chinese elite athletes , as well as coaches and team officials, found that cultural attitudes and sporting environments could influence whether athletes sought help. Participants spoke about issues including depressed mood, competition anxiety and sleep problems, while stigma – including fears of being regarded as weak – was among the barriers identified. Athletes were often more comfortable turning first to teammates, friends or parents than to formal mental-health services.
Kenya’s Wilfred Bungei recognises some of that from his own experience. The 2008 Olympic 800m champion has spoken openly about his problems with alcohol and mental health after his competitive career ended.
Wilfred Bungei in action at the 2008 Olympics (© Getty Images)
Among his wake-up calls were missing important engagements because he had been drinking, and realising that his children were uncomfortable being in the car with him when they knew he was drunk. Looking back 10 years or more, Bungei says alcoholism and mental-health problems in Kenya were often seen as matters of personal choice.
“People with mental-health problems were stigmatised,” he says. He believes attitudes have improved since then and there is now more empathy, although some of that stigma remains.
“The talk behind the scenes doesn’t indicate a society that has fully embraced mental-health issues,” he says. “Most people would rather suffer from the inside than be open.”
For Bungei, his family was crucial in recognising that he needed help. “Family is the first pillar,” he says. “If one’s family accepts that this person is sick and needs help, the individual wouldn’t care much about what society says because they know, ‘I have people who care’.”
He has sometimes compared alcoholism with diabetes when trying to explain to people that addiction is an illness rather than simply a personal failing. “The first thing is accept who you are and don’t care about the noise,” he says.
Bungei also believes athletes need more help preparing for life after competition. “Athletes retire early in life and they have money and plenty of free time,” he says. “Remember, athletes live a strict life 365 days a year as sportsmen and women.”
He says there is still no clear roadmap in Kenya to help athletes cope with that transition. He has, however, since found another role within the sport. Through his work with the World Athletics Media Academy, he says he has regained a sense of “purpose and responsibility” from training as a commentator.
He hopes eventually to use that platform to speak more widely about mental-health issues affecting sportsmen and women in African countries, and what could be done to support them.
Singapore’s Shanti Pereira has spoken about a different kind of mental struggle during the years between her early breakthrough and her rise to the top of Asian sprinting.
Sprinter Shanti Pereira of Singapore (© Getty Images)
After winning the SEA Games 200m title on home soil in 2015, Pereira found it difficult to deal with the expectations that followed. Results stalled, injuries followed and, in 2018, she lost both her Sport Excellence Scholarship and her university scholarship within the space of a week.
Speaking to CNA in 2022, she said that physically she still felt capable of running personal and national records, “but mentally I wasn’t there”.
“There was a lot of self-doubt that kind of grew as the years went by,” she said. At times she lost her motivation and became afraid of performing badly

articles.title_orig: When could Zverev reach World No. 1 for the first time?
articles.title_zh: When could Zverev reach World No. 1 for the first time?
articles.content_orig:
When can Alexander Zverev climb to the No. 1 spot in the PIF ATP Rankings and become the 30th member of the prestigious ATP No. 1 Club?
Zverev currently holds 9,720 points in the PIF ATP Live Rankings, trailing current World No. 1 Jannik Sinner by 1,230 points.
With Sinner ending his 2026 season due to injury, there are two paths for the German to reach the top spot as early as 2 November.
Zverev would become the World No. 1 by winning the Rolex Shanghai Masters crown and reaching the semi-finals of the ATP 500 event in Vienna.
Alternatively, the 29-year-old would also secure the top ranking by reaching the Shanghai final and winning the title in Vienna.
Zverev first broke into the Top 10 in May 2017 and reached a career-high World No. 2 for the first in June 2022. If successful in his bid to become the World No. 1, Zverev would become only the second German player to reach the pinnacle of the PIF ATP Rankings, after Boris Becker in 1991.
A two-time Nitto ATP Finals champion, Zverev would become the newest member of the ATP No. 1 Club since Sinner in June 2024.

articles.title_orig: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
articles.title_zh: Eritrea asks UN to intervene in standoff with Ethiopia
articles.content_orig:
Eritrea has asked the United Nations to take “deterrent measures” after what it called Ethiopia’s “declaration of war” in the conflict over the Tigray region.
Eritrea’s request comes a day after Addis Ababa, in a letter to the Security Council, accused Asmara of launching an “all-out invasion”, saying Eritrean troops had advanced up to 60 kilometres (37 miles) into Ethiopia’s Tigray.
In a separate letter to the council on Saturday, Eritrean Foreign Minister Osman Saleh said the claims of an Eritrean incursion were part of an Ethiopian plan to justify a war of aggression and urged the UN to intervene, invoking Chapter VII of the UN Charter, which allows measures from sanctions to military action.
The neighbouring countries have accused each other of starting a war over Tigray, where Ethiopia says Eritrea is backing rebels.
An alliance of seven armed groups launched attacks against federal Ethiopian forces in the northern region last month, as they attempt to overthrow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.
Eritrean forces have since reportedly intruded into Ethiopian territory, with Addis Ababa accusing Asmara of backing the rebel Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF).
The Ethiopian army pushed TPLF rebels back this week and seized the region’s capital, Mekelle. It also said it launched drone strikes against Eritrean troops in the region.
“Eritrea requests the UN Security Council to forcefully condemn Ethiopia’s deplorable declaration of war against Eritrea … and take the requisite deterrent measures,” Eritrea’s Saleh said in the letter on Saturday.
He said Ethiopia’s action would cause “huge devastation to the peoples of both countries and destabilise the whole region”.
Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos on Friday accused Eritrea of “a blatant act of aggression that engages Ethiopia’s inherent right to self-defence”.
Timothewos invoked Ethiopia’s right to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, but he did not specify what measures the country was taking.
Faisal Roble, a Horn of Africa specialist, believes both sides are “preparing for the last phase of an open conflict”.
“There is really no doubt that both of them are inching towards an open conflict,” he told Al Jazeera from the Kenyan capital, Nairobi.
“Whatever they write to the United Nations, it is just posturing and making sure that they have some sort of international support on their side,” the analyst added.
In his letter, Saleh called Ethiopia’s actions “deceitful attempts to rationalise its brazen acts of war”, claiming that they were “hollow in substance”.
Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel accused Ethiopia on Friday of pursuing aggression against Eritrea through its demands for sovereign access to the Red Sea. Writing on X, he did not explicitly confirm or deny the reported troop crossings.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy reiterated on Monday that Ethiopia must have access to the Red Sea.
Eritrea gained independence from Ethiopia in 1993, and they fought a deadly border war from 1998 to 2000.
Relations improved after Abiy came to power in 2018, but have soured again in recent years.
Landlocked Ethiopia has repeatedly insisted that it has a right to direct sea access, which Eritrea interprets as a threat to invade and seize its port at Assab.
TPLF fighters battled Ethiopian government forces, then backed by Eritrea, in a devastating 2020-2022 war.

articles.title_orig: Pope Leo declares death penalty ‘inadmissible’ as his native U.S. plans to livestream execution
articles.title_zh: Pope Leo declares death penalty ‘inadmissible’ as his native U.S. plans to livestream execution
articles.content_orig:
ROME — Pope Leo XIV on Saturday declared capital punishment “inadmissible” as he marked the World Day Against the Death Penalty and his native United States announced plans to livestream an execution by firing squad.
In a post on X, the American pope quoted the revised Catholic teaching on capital punishment ushered in by Pope Francis that the death penalty attacks the inherent dignity of a human being.
“The common good can be safeguarded and the requirements of justice can be met without recourse to capital punishment,” read the post under Leo’s official handle, @Pontifex. “Effective systems of detention have been developed that protect citizens while at the same time do not completely deprive those who are guilty of the possibility of redemption.”
The post ended with the hashtag #NoDeathPenalty.
The U.S. Defense Department announced Thursday that the firing squad execution of Nidal Malik Hasan, convicted of a 2009 shooting at the Fort Hood military base, will be livestreamed. Hasan, scheduled to be executed at Fort Hood on Dec. 3, was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others.
Why Hegseth's decision to livestream execution is raising questions
Leo didn’t refer specifically to the planned execution, or the botched lethal injection in Tennessee last week that has revived debate over the death penalty in the United States. Saturday is World Day Against the Death Penalty, and it is common for the pope’s official social media accounts to post messages marking such commemorations.
But Leo’s post came just hours after his top deputy, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said explicitly that the planned U.S. public execution was “unacceptable.”
Pope Francis in 2018 amended official Catholic teaching to declare capital punishment “inadmissible” in all circumstances.
Previously, the Catechism of the Catholic Church, the official compendium of church teaching, said the church didn’t exclude recourse to capital punishment “if this is the only possible way of effectively defending human lives against the unjust aggressor.”
Past popes had upheld that position, though St. John Paul II began urging an end to the practice and stressed that guilty people were just as deserving of dignity as innocent ones.
Like Francis before him, Leo has made visiting prisons a key part of his papal travel in a bid to give a message of hope to inmates and underscore their inherent dignity, that God loves them and that there is always a chance for redemption.
“If any of you fear being abandoned by everyone, know that God will never abandon you, and that the church will stand by your side,” Leo told inmates at the notorious Bata prison in Equatorial Guinea during his visit in April. Leo is to visit a prison in Buenos Aires during his upcoming tour through Latin America.
Pope Leo asked if he helped with historic White Sox turnaround
Speaking specifically about the United States, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said the planned livestreamed execution was “truly incomprehensible” and “unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle.”
“The Church’s position is one of total opposition to the death penalty; it is incompatible with human dignity and serves as no deterrent—,” Parolin said in comments carried by Vatican News. “It is truly incomprehensible that anyone would want to use this system today — I don’t know for what purpose. It is certainly unacceptable to turn death into a spectacle; even if the person is guilty, of course, there are other methods.”
The head of the U.S. bishops conference, Archbishop Paul Coakley, expressed “shock” and “great sorrow” at the Pentagon’s plans.
“In no way can Hasan’s actions be condoned but this decision is a barbaric promotion of a culture of death and must be reconsidered,” he said in a statement Friday. “The public execution even of one who has done grave harm will only further undermine the moral fabric of our nation and be a blight on the conscience of its people.”

articles.title_orig: +78 kg: At 19, Hyeonji Lee Has World Titles at All Levels
articles.title_zh: +78 kg: At 19, Hyeonji Lee Has World Titles at All Levels
articles.content_orig:
For the first 2 minutes and 10 seconds Dicko was leading on attacks and looked to be ready to take the win at any moment. Faster to her favourite grip, attacking without hesitation, Dicko looked back at her best form.
However, Hyeonji Lee is as explosive as they come, all her power going into every technique. She turned in with a huge harai-goshi and threw for a waza-ari, transitioning to the osaekomi without delay. Dicko was unable to do anything against the young Korean and as the ten seconds needed to convert her first score to ippon ticked by, both judoka knew the outcome was set.
After the final Lee said, "I am so thrilled to win this world championship title. I feel I managed to deliver a complete and polished performance today. Facing Romane Dicko in the final was a first for me, I felt very nervous beforehand. However, I know I perform well against unfamiliar opponents, so I trusted my abilities and stuck to my own style throughout the contest. It is an immense source of pride to bring this gold medal home to South Korea."
World cadet champion in 2023, world junior champion in 2024 and now the senior world title also belongs to Hyeonji Lee. This teenager is taking on the world and winning!
The left versus right situation gave rise to interesting attacks and the possibility for well-practised counters but in this battle Ivanova was more determined.
Asya Tavano attacked with a right-handed uchi-mata, to no avail. Ivanova then mirrored her and put in her own uchi-mata, on the left, but with greater confidence. She drove the Italian to the floor for a yuko and transitioned directly into the hold which she kept until the referee, Mr Olivier Desroses, called ‘ippon.’ Mariia Ivanova was not among the favourites at the beginning of the day but she worked hard for her medal and will be a new name to be wary of as the next competitions come along.
For the first four minutes this was a very close contest but with moments that looked to be going Helena Vukovic’s way. She attacked well and neutralised the preferred gripping of the world number one.
As soon as the golden score period began, with only a shido apiece on the scoreboard, Raz found a new gear altogether. She attacked with her seoi-otoshi and rolled through it perfectly to score ippon and earn her place on the podium. This is Hershko’s second world championship medal.
