articles.title_orig: Trump Announces White House Inquiry Into Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.title_zh: Trump Announces White House Inquiry Into Fed Governor Lisa Cook
articles.content_orig:
WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump opened another chapter in his effort to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook Friday by establishing a "committee of inquiry" to investigate allegations that she made false statements in mortgage applications.
The inquiry will include a hearing at the White House Nov. 5, Trump said in a written memo , that Cook "shall" attend to answer questions from the committee. The hearing wouldn't be public but a transcript would be published, the memo said.
Trump's extraordinary demand that Cook testify before the committee will likely renew concerns about threats to the Federal Reserve's independence. The president has repeatedly called for the central bank to cut its key interest rate, but just last month, the Fed raised it instead , led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, whom Trump appointed earlier this year.
Trump's attempts to fire Cook from the Fed's seven-member board of governors represent the first time in the central bank's 113-year history that a president has sought to remove a Fed governor. Cook was appointed by former President Joe Biden and is the first Black woman on the Fed's board. Trump's attacks on her followed other efforts to oust or indict Black officials , such as New York Attorney General Letitia James and Gen. Charles Q. Brown, the former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
"As President, it is my job to ensure the laws are faithfully executed, including by firing subordinates who cannot be trusted to tell the truth and follow the law," Trump wrote in the memorandum.
Cook's attorneys, Abbe Lowell and Norman Eisen, said they were considering having Cook appear at the Nov. 5 hearing and respond to the charges.
"We have engaged with the White House to evaluate whether the process proposed has a possibility of being a genuine one and not simply a box checking exercise," Lowell and Eisen said in a statement. "Governor Cook welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her."
The "committee of inquiry" will be composed of Kevin Hassett, the president's top economic adviser, who has frequently echoed Trump's criticisms of the Fed; Keith Sonderling, the acting director of the Office of Government Ethics, whom the president has also appointed to lead the Labor Department, and Andrea Lucas, the chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, whom Trump appointed in November 2025.
Trump initially tried to fire Cook in August 2025 after alleging she had committed mortgage fraud by declaring two different properties to be her "primary" residence in mortgage applications in 2021. Mortgages on primary homes can often receive a lower interest rate or other beneficial terms.
Cook has denied any wrongdoing and has not been charged with a crime. Lowell and Eisen have previously said Cook committed an "inadvertent error" and did refer to one of the properties as a vacation home in other documents.
"An inadvertent error is not fraud, as the President and a third of his cabinet should know because they reportedly did the same thing," Lowell and Eisen said in August.
The Federal Reserve declined to comment on Trump's announcement.
Trump and some of his economic advisers have blamed the Fed's broader rate-setting committee, which includes 12 voting members and 19 officials in total, for forcing last month's rate hike, even though it followed comments by Warsh in August that signaled higher rates were likely. As a member of the board of governors, Cook is also one of the 12 voting members of the committee. The vote to lift rates Sept. 16 was unanimous .
The move also follows a Supreme Court ruling in June that Cook could keep her job after Trump sought to fire her last year. That ruling included a footnote that said nothing prevented Trump from "trying again" as long as she was given proper notice and an opportunity to respond to the charges.
Trump said the committee of inquiry will seek to establish whether there is "cause" to fire Cook, as required under the law governing the Fed. The Supreme Court said in June that a for-cause firing required an alleged offense that was serious and related to an official's job.
Scott Alvarez, formerly the chief counsel for the Fed, said that President William Howard Taft set up a similar commission in 1912 to remove two officials from an independent agency. The commission created by Trump goes beyond the type of process the Supreme Court said was needed to fire Cook.
"It's an attempt to show that he's really giving Cook as much process as possible," Alvarez said.
Still, the allegations against Cook don't appear to meet the "for cause" standard set out by the Supreme Court, Alvarez said.
Other analysts said that Trump will likely use the process to ultimately fire Cook.
"We do not see why the White House would start this process if it were not trying to create a way to justify removing Cook from her job," Jaret Seiberg, managing director of TD Cowen's Washington Research Group, said in a note to clients.

articles.title_orig: Public warned about possible measles exposure at several Chester County, Pennsylvania stores
articles.title_zh: Public warned about possible measles exposure at several Chester County, Pennsylvania stores
articles.content_orig:
WEST GROVE, Pa. (WPVI) -- The Chester County Health Department is warning the public of a possible measles exposure at several local stores.
The possible exposure happened on Sunday, Oct. 4, at the following locations:
-CVS at 870 Baltimore Pike, Kennett Square, 19348; between 10:45 a.m. and 3 p.m.
-CVS at 857 West Baltimore Pike, West Grove, 19390; between 12:30 p.m. and 3:30 p.m.
-Giant at 849 Baltimore Pike, West Grove, 19390; between 1 p.m. and 3:45 p.m.
A person infected with measles visited those locations while contagious, county health officials said.
RELATED: Measles cases surpass 1,000 in Pennsylvania amid the state's largest outbreak in decades
Anyone at those locations is urged to check whether they are immune to measles.
The health department said you are considered immune against measles if any of the following apply to you:
-Have already had measles, or
-Have received at least one of the two doses of measles-containing vaccine (usually given as measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine).
People who aren't protected against measles can get the virus up to two hours after someone with measles left the same room or airspace, health officials said.
This incident comes amid a historic measles outbreaking Pennsylvania, with more than 1,000 cases reported.
For more information, visit Chesco.org/Measles .

articles.title_orig: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.title_zh: China and Europe Step Back From Trade War With Limits on Chinese Car Exports
articles.content_orig:
The agreement will see Chinese hybrid vehicle exports decline by ‘several million cars’ in the coming years, EU trade chief says
The European Union and China have “reached an understanding” that will cut Chinese hybrid car shipments to the bloc by “more than a half”, in a temporary salve to trade tensions that have threatened to boil over into a full-blown trade war.
Speaking after marathon trade talks in Beijing, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic said the deal would see China slash its hybrid car exports “by several million cars” over a four-year period.
“This is the first time that China has accepted to moderate its exports without going through the phase of prior trade tensions, and I very much appreciate that,” Sefcovic told reporters in the Chinese capital.
The sides also agreed to expedite EU applications for rare earth mineral export licences and improve market access for goods including car parts, olive oil and textiles, which Sefcovic said could be worth “almost €4 billion” (US$4.5 billion) in current export value.

articles.title_orig: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
articles.title_zh: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner
articles.content_orig:
Last month we covered the winner of Nikon’s Small World in Motion video: Ning Xu of Tsinghua University in China, whose video captured tiny cilia beating in the airways of a child with a rare respiratory disorder. But allegations surfaced about Xu’s use of AI while making the video. Nikon launched an investigation and concluded that Xu’s entry did not comply with competition rules. The new winner is Nguyen Nam Nhat of Vietnam with a video of a tiny roundworm and a single-celled organism (above).
According to a BBC report, some researchers expressed concern that Xu’s video had structural abnormalities and that cell features appeared and disappeared in a way one would not see in actual cellular biology. Others spotted what looked like AI watermarks embedded within the source files. Xu said he used AI “to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images”; however, he denied that AI was used “to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion.”
Founded in 2011, the Nikon Small World in Motion competition is a spinoff of the company’s Small World Photomicrography Competition, which has been around since 1974. Both are meant “to showcase the beauty and complexity of things seen through the light microscope”—one through still photographs, the other through photovideography, taking advantage of all the technological advances that now allow users to make movies or time-lapse images through the microscope.
The other winners also moved up a notch with Xu’s disqualification. Benedikt Pleyer of Bavaria, Germany, placed second with a video of jellyfish larvae suspended in water droplets; Andrew Moore of Howard Hughes Medical Institute in the US placed third with a video of synchronized cell division in neighboring cells; Patrick Hickey of Hypha Research Ltd. in Edinburgh, Scotland, placed fourth with a video of the dynamics of mitochondria and chloroplasts in Turtle Vine leaf cells; and Igor Adameyko placed fifth with a video of a tiny, colorful sea slug ( Cyerce kikutarobabai ) on the move.
Here is Nikon’s full statement:
After thoroughly re-evaluating the video and supporting materials and consulting with members of our judging panel, Nikon has determined that the winning video did not comply with the competition rules regarding generative AI. Nikon has adjusted the competition rankings on our website to reflect this decision.
This decision is based solely on the submitted video’s eligibility under the rules outlined for this competition. It should not be interpreted as a judgment of the entrant’s professional reputation, scientific contributions, or intent.
Advances in imaging and artificial intelligence continue to evolve rapidly, creating new challenges for organizations across many fields. This event has shown the need for Nikon Small World and Nikon Small World in Motion to revisit rules and evaluation procedures for future competition entries.
The Nikon Small World and Nikon Small World in Motion competitions celebrate excellence in imaging, both scientific and artistic in nature. We value the integrity of each image and video selected to appear in our winning galleries, and remain committed to upholding the standards of excellence that have defined this competition.
_src_links: AI disqualification yields new Nikon Small World in Motion winner

articles.title_orig: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, damaging buildings and injuring at least 27
articles.title_zh: Powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, damaging buildings and injuring at least 27
articles.content_orig:
A powerful 7.7-magnitude earthquake struck Panama on Friday, damaging buildings and triggering evacuations, according to the US Geological Survey (USGS).
The quake's epicentre was located near the country's southern tip, around 12 kilometres west-southwest of the remote community of Pitaloza Arriba, the USGS said.
A tsunami warning was issued on Friday for the eastern Pacific, but this was later lifted.
Rene Garcia, the head of emergency operations at the country's National Civil Protection System, told the AFP news agency that there were so far no reported fatalities. At least 27 people have reportedly been injured.
Tremors were felt in the capital Panama City, where buildings shook and residents rushed into the streets as they awaited updates.
Omar Smith of the National Civil Protection Service told local broadcaster Telemetro Reporta that damage had mainly been reported in the central provinces of Veraguas, Herrera and Los Santos. He said no damage had been reported in the capital.
Several aftershocks followed the first tremor.
Local media reported that the quake was also felt in parts of neighbouring Colombia.
Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino urged calm following the earthquake, writing on X: “What happened should not be used to cause alarm or disorder.”
Panama is located along the Pacific "Ring of Fire", a 40,000-kilometre stretch of volcanoes and fault lines where most of the world's earthquakes occur.

articles.title_orig: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.title_zh: Top Democratic Group Pumps Millions Into Kansas Senate Race
articles.content_orig:
Democrats are dreaming of a revolution in Kansas in November, trying to believe in polling that shows a tight race in the Senate contest there between the Democrat, Rev. Adam Hamilton, and the Republican incumbent, Sen. Roger Marshall.
It would indeed be a watershed moment if Hamilton takes the seat: No Democrat has won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, not quite a century but a very, very long time.
In fact, since Kansas became a state in 1861, only three Democrats have represented it in the Senate. It’s a remarkable statistic since the two parties have evolved so much during that time.
Related: Read a Q and A with a Kansas-based political expert from CNN’s What Matters newsletter about why Kansas has stayed Republican at the Senate level for so long and why Kansans feel targeted by some of Trump’s policies this year.
While American politics seem locked in place; 30 of the 50 states have been represented by a senator from both parties during this century. And while the states that have been represented by both parties most recently track closely with the swing states that decide elections, there are a few exceptions, like Montana and Alabama.
No Republican has been elected to represent the islands since 1970. That Republican, Hiram Fong, was one of Hawaii’s two first senators, elected when Hawaii became a state in 1959. No Democrat has been elected to represent Wyoming or Utah since that same year.
The longest streak east of the Mississippi River is in New Jersey, where no Republican has been elected to the US Senate since Clifford Case was elected in 1972, capping a long career on Capitol Hill. A Republican senator, Jeffrey Chiesa, was briefly appointed to serve in 2013. That was the result of the state having a Republican governor, Chris Christie, at the time.
The Senate is up for grabs. Plot each party’s best path to winning
A Kansas voter would have to be well over 100 years old to have voted for the state’s last Democratic senator, but the current governor is a Democrat.
In New Hampshire, the state is represented by two Democratic senators. The last Republican elected was Kelly Ayotte in 2010. She’s currently the state’s governor. And Republicans hope that another former senator, John Sununu, can break the trend and reclaim a Senate seat this year. When he served as senator, the state had two Republican senators.
Far fewer states are sending a split delegation — both a Republican and a Democratic senator — than ever before in US history. Since the nationwide election of senators began with the 1914 election after the ratification of the 17th amendment, there have generally been at least 10 and frequently more than 20 split delegations, according to a 2021 analysis by Pew .
Currently there are only four: Vermont, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin — none of which has a Senate race this year — and Maine, where Republican Sen. Susan Collins is among the most endangered incumbents. If she loses to Democrat Troy Jackson, Maine will join the wave of states bringing their senators in line with their status as blue or red for presidential purposes. And Collins is one of the few true moderates of either party left in the chamber.
The other senator from Maine, Angus King, is an independent, but like Sen. Bernie Sanders in Vermont, he sides with Democrats in procedural matters, making him a Democrat for purposes of determining which party controls the Senate.
The last time Vermont elected a Republican, Sen. Jim Jeffords in 2000, he ended up switching parties when Republicans angered him. There’s conjecture now that Pennsylvania’s Democratic Sen. John Fetterman might soon do the inverse, but he has insisted that he will remain a Democrat.
There’s Pennsylvania precedent for party-switching. Sen. Arlen Specter went from R to D in 2009.
These rural Democrat and Republican voters have a message for Washington
The last Democrat elected to the Senate from Texas was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988. He resigned to be in President Bill Clinton’s Cabinet. 1988, coincidentally, is the last year California elected a Republican. It does not feel close — or not as close as Texas — to electing someone from the out-of-power party, but things are changing all the time.
Both Dakotas and Montana were represented by two Democrats within the last 25 years. Now all three are represented by two Republicans, although this year in Montana and South Dakota it is independents, not even Democrats, who are mounting the biggest challenge to Republicans.
The independent who seems to have the best chance of winning at the moment is in Nebraska, where Dan Osborn is challenging Sen. Pete Ricketts. A Democrat last won in Nebraska in 2006.
There are a lot of reasons that running as an independent is tricky in American politics, especially at the state or national level. Osborn’s success might not turn into a Senate seat, but it is a clear message that there are states where party brands are so badly damaged that shedding them could be the best path to unseating an entrenched in-party power. But it’s also true that as the parties change and shift, tectonic moves mean their time in power is ultimately limited.

articles.title_orig: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.title_zh: Class action alleges Webull misled investors about China operations
articles.content_orig:
A class action accuses Webull of hiding the real scale of its China operations from investors.
A securities complaint filed October 8 in federal court in Tampa, Florida, alleges online broker-dealer Webull Corporation told investors one story about its ties to mainland China while the reality, according to the filing, was very different.
The complaint, Ward v. Webull Corporation et al. (Case No. 8:26-cv-03052), brings claims under federal securities laws - specifically Sections 10(b) and 20(a) of the Securities Exchange Act and SEC Rule 10b-5. It names Webull - a Cayman Islands-incorporated broker-dealer whose shares trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker "BULL" - along with the company's founder and CEO, and its CFO, as defendants.
The company describes itself as a broker-dealer regulated in 12 major markets globally, with US offices in St. Petersburg, Florida.
The case centers on a string of SEC filings the complaint alleges painted an incomplete picture. In its 2024 annual report, a July 2025 registration statement, and its 2025 annual report, Webull told investors its "operations in mainland China are limited to research and development and technical support functions," according to the complaint. Those filings also stated that US customer data "cannot be transmitted outside of the United States or accessed by our non-U.S. employees without permission and oversight from our U.S. personnel."
The complaint alleges those statements were "false and/or misleading." In reality, the filing claims, "Webull's core platform, software development, data pipelines, and core engineering depended on PRC-based personnel and on technology infrastructure subject to Chinese law."
More broadly, the complaint alleges that "Webull's ownership structure, technical workforce, technology infrastructure, cross-border data routing, financing, and compliance structure were structurally tied to China" - contradicting the company's assurances that its main business operations were US-based.
The numbers in Webull's own filings tell the story. The complaint points to the company's July 2025 registration statement, which disclosed that its mainland China subsidiary, Hunan Weibu Information Technology Co., Ltd., "employs 731 employees, representing 61% of our employees as of December 31, 2024." By the end of 2025, the complaint alleges, that figure had climbed to 863 employees - 62% of Webull's global workforce.
The complaint also alleges that the US House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party delivered a letter to the CEO of Webull Financial - the company's US broker-dealer arm - in December 2024, seeking information about the relationship between Webull Financial and Webull's China operations, and about the security of customer data.
According to the complaint, Webull's SEC filings characterized the Select Committee's concerns as "largely based on outdated and inaccurate information."
That position became harder to hold on October 7, 2026. The complaint alleges that before markets opened, CNBC reported the Select Committee had found a "profound gap" between how Webull presented itself as an American company and its actual control and operations. The committee also reportedly found that Webull "initially told the Select Committee that it had no offices or employees in China," the complaint alleges.
Webull's stock dropped sharply. The complaint alleges the company's Class A ordinary shares fell $1.39 per share - approximately 19% - to close at $5.89 on unusually heavy trading volume.
The complaint alleges the company's founder and CEO - a citizen of the People's Republic of China who, as of March 31, 2026, held approximately 79.2% of total voting power - "knew or recklessly disregarded" the extent of Webull's dependence on China-based operations.
For advisors and compliance teams, this complaint is worth watching. The allegations raise questions about due diligence on broker-dealer platforms with complex cross-border structures - and about what happens when a company's SEC filings and a congressional investigation tell different stories about where operations actually sit.
The allegations in this complaint have not been tested in court. No court has ruled on the merits of the case.

articles.title_orig: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.title_zh: Nitrogen leads solid Casse quartet at Breeders’ Cup World Championships
articles.content_orig:
D.J. Stable’s Kentucky homebred Nitrogen will make her third appearance at the Breeders’ Cup World Championships when she headlines a talented field in the Grade 1, $2 million Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
Trained by dual Hall of Famer Mark Casse, the 4-year-old Medaglia d’Oro bay made her last three outings in New York, including a pair of memorable Grade 1 starts at Saratoga Race Course with a 12 3/4-length romp in the Ogden Phipps presented by Ford and a runner-up effort to reigning Horse of the Year Sovereignty while facing males in the Whitney.
Her Ogden Phipps effort earned a career-best 113 Beyer Speed Figure with the Chad Brown-trained runner-up Fully Subscribed exiting that race to win three graded events, including a pair of Grade 1s.
Nitrogen had her final Breeders’ Cup prep at Belmont Park, wiring a field of five to score by 2 3/4-lengths under regular rider Jose Ortiz in the Grade 2 Beldame on September 25.
“We shipped her down to Kentucky on Wednesday and she trained this morning at Keeneland. She's doing well,” Casse said. “I thought the Beldame was a good race. I liked the timing. It looks like a showdown between her and Chad's filly.”
Casse said he has no intention of dulling Nitrogen’s abundant early foot in a Distaff field expected to have other potential pace types.
“She'll be pretty close. We may slow her down a little bit but we're not going to take hold of her. We're going to let her do her thing,” Casse said.
Nitrogen has banked in excess of $3 million through an 18-9-6-3 record that includes a trio of graded wins on turf and five graded wins on dirt. Her previous Breeders’ Cup attempts came at Del Mar, including a closing third as a maiden in the 2024 Grade 1 Juvenile Fillies Turf and a runner-up try to Scylla in last year’s Distaff.
While Casse hopes she can go one better in the Distaff at Keeneland, he’s buoyed by the fact that D. J. Stable plans to bring back the reigning Champion 3-Year-Old Filly for another season of racing next year.
“That's the plan as long as she's healthy out of the Breeders' Cup,” Casse said. “Our sport needs its stars and she's definitely a star. I commend the Greens for being the sportsmen they are.”
Gary Barber, Bridlewood Farm and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ late-running Measure has hit the board in each of her last four outings – the last three in Grade 1 company – and will look to capitalize on a potential pace battle in the Breeders’ Cup Distaff.
The 3-year-old daughter of Essential Quality finished third in the nine-furlong Grade 1 Coaching Club American Oaks won by stablemate Counting Stars in July at Saratoga to begin her streak of top-flight tilts. She followed with a neck second to My Gun's Loaded in the Spa’s 10-furlong Alabama presented by Keeneland Sales on August 22 ahead of a closing third in the 1 1/16-mile Cotillion on September 19 at Parx when in tight approaching the three-eighths.
“She's a filly that we were high on from the beginning. I wasn't that disappointed with her earlier on in the year, I just thought she needed to get her act together and needed some pace,” Casse said. “Her Alabama was a huge race, and she got very unlucky in the Cotillion. She'll enjoy the mile and an eighth and will also enjoy a hot pace, which looking at the Distaff it's looking like it will be fairly lively.”
Manny Franco will retain the mount on Measure.
Gary Barber, Blue Crevalle Racing and Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ Classic Q was initially considered for a Breeders’ Cup start versus males in the Grade 1 Mile but will instead target the Grade 1 Filly and Mare Turf.
The 4-year-old Classic Empire grey has won 3-of-6 starts this year, including frontrunning scores in the Grade 2 Distaff Turf Mile in May at Churchill Downs and the Grade 1 Just a Game presented by Resolute Racing on June 6 at Saratoga. She secured her second career Grade 1 last out with a stalking nose score over Lush Lips in the one-mile First Lady on October 3 at Keeneland.
“We thought about the Mile but we're going to run her against the girls,” Casse said. “I would think with the mile and three-sixteenths that more than likely she'll be on the lead.”
Hall of Famer Javier Castellano takes over aboard Classic Q from fellow Hall of Famer John Velazquez, who is committed to Gimma a Nother.
D.J. Stable will also be represented by Voyager in the Grade 1 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile Fillies Turf.
The Justify bay ran second in her first two outings on dirt, including a runner-up try to Harper’s Corner in the Listed Schuylerville on July 3 at the Spa.
Voyager then shifted to the Saratoga turf on August 1 and stretched out to a two-turn 1 1/16-miles to post a frontrunning nose score over Correlation Trade. The third-place finisher of that event, Bittersweet Memory, exited to graduate at Saratoga and followed with a fourth-place run in the Grade 2 Miss Grillo here last weekend.
Voyager enters the Breeders’ Cup from a 1 1/4-length win in the Grade 1 Natalma contested at a one-turn mile over firm E.P. Taylor turf on September 12 at Woodbine.
Casse said the Spa turf experience will be beneficial for Voyager as she goes back to two turns for the one-mile Juvenile Fillies Turf.
“When she broke her maiden at Saratoga, I was happy because we were able to get a two-turn race into her. We went back to one-turn for the Natalma, but I feel she's very versatile. Her race in the Natalma was really good and she's training really well,” Casse said.
Casse enjoyed a winning barn debut Thursday for world-traveler Facteur Cheval , who scored by a half-length under Irad Ortiz, Jr. in a 1 1/16-mile Keeneland allowance for owners Team Valor International and Gary Barber.
The 7-year-old Ribchester gelding has banked in excess of $5.7 million through a 28-7-7-6 ledger topped by a win in the 2024 Group 1 Dubai Turf. He landed a deep-closing sixth in the Grade 3 Mint Millions on September 7 at Kentucky Downs for his former trainer Jerome Reynier.
“We took him over right after that race. Barry [Irwin] had mentioned to us going into yesterday's race that you need to get him into the race,” Casse said. “We let Irad know you need to be aggressive early on with him and get him into the race and you saw that yesterday. It made the difference. It's a privilege to have that horse in the barn.”
Facteur Cheval will point to the Grade 3 River City on November 7 at Churchill Downs.
Casse enjoyed his second win at the new Belmont Park on Wednesday when Gary Barber’s Ori wired a one-mile turf starter optional-claimer in her first start for new connections after being haltered for $45,000 from an optional-claiming win in September at Saratoga.
With Castellano aboard, the 5-year-old Hard Spun chestnut zipped through splits of 22.39 seconds, 45.09 and 1:09.48 en route to a 6 1/4-length score in 1:33.35. The winning effort returned an 86 Beyer – four points shy of a career-best 90 earned from a runner-up try in the 2024 Listed Winter Memories at Belmont at the Big A.
Ori is out of the stakes-winning Pioneerof the Nile mare Princessof the Nyl. Her stakes-winning third dam, Arabis, is a full-sister to multiple graded stakes-winner Atelier and a half-sister to Grade 1-winner Aldiza.
“We don't claim very many. She's unique in that we thought she looked like she had ability running, but we also claimed her to be a broodmare,” Casse said. “If she keeps running the way she ran the other day, she may run another year.
“Javi called me after the race and said, 'she was impressive.' Normally I call him, but he called me,” Casse added, with a laugh.
Ori will likely point to the Listed $175,000 Noble Damsel, a one-mile turf test for fillies and mares 3-years-old and up on November 27 here.
Casse indicated he will have a big presence in New York this winter for a meet that will be contested exclusively over Tapeta. His significant stock will include a number of horses with past Tapeta experience at Woodbine, whose season comes to a close on December 13.

articles.title_zh: Measles confirmed in local school
articles.content_orig:
Measles has been confirmed in a local school.
Eden Christian Academy said Friday that it’s working with the Allegheny County Health Department (ACHD) to stop the disease’s spread after being notified of measles in its community.
Two measles cases were confirmed in Allegheny County this week, on Monday and Thursday. ACHD says both people attend the same school but live in different households.
Eden Christian Academy would not share details about any patients, but said it is addressing the issue across its three campuses.
Actions include communicating with families and staff who may have been exposed, deep cleaning across all facilities and advising unvaccinated or non-immune staff and students about “exclusion periods,” according to public health guidelines.
The school adds that its health records and policies are compliant with the state’s student vaccination requirements.
Pennsylvania’s measles outbreak, which has surpassed 1,000 cases this year, is the largest state outbreak in more than three decades, the Associated Press reports .

articles.title_zh: Jackson County prepares for world’s biggest earthquake drill on Thursday
articles.content_orig:
Published 11:03 am Friday, October 9, 2026
Jackson County is asking residents to prepare for the Great ShakeOut, the world’s largest earthquake drill scheduled for 10:15 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 15.
Millions of individuals across the globe will practice Drop, Cover and Hold On, the official safety procedure to protect oneself during an earthquake.
This annual event provides an opportunity for people in homes, schools and businesses to assess their disaster preparedness, improve their emergency safety plans and practice what to do in the event of a real earthquake.
For more information and resources to plan your drill, visit shakeout.org/Oregon .
Completing a few small tasks ahead of time, such as assembling a basic emergency supply kit and determining your shelter strategy, helps to assure that you and your family will know what to do and have the supplies you need to be safe wherever you are.
For more preparedness resources and tips, visit ready.gov .
Jackson County will also be conducting a test of the Jackson Alerts notification system in conjunction with the Great ShakeOut.
This service provides critical information quickly for a variety of emergency situations.
To raise awareness and educate the public on disaster preparedness, residents registered with Jackson Alerts will receive a test alert through all listed delivery methods — call, text and email — between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m.
Register, update your Jackson Alerts account and/or find more information at jacksoncountyor.gov/alerts .

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
When Bose proclaimed that the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar was its "loudest, deepest and most immersive" model yet, I still assumed it would need a subwoofer." Yet when I first connected the company's latest soundbar to my TV, I quickly realized it didn't need the extra bass boost. The combination of CleanBass tech and QuietPort acoustics provide enough low-end tone that you aren't likely to crave an additional, pricey sub. Since the soundbar alone is already $1,099 , that was a welcome surprise.
I get it: There's not a ton of room for innovation when it comes to the design of soundbars. They all have to be elongated and rectangular to be able to contain a collection of drivers without blocking your TV. But there is room for improvement when it comes to the general look of soundbars, and that's where Bose stepped up its game on the Lifestyle Ultra.
The speaker is short and wide, just like you'd expect, but the textured, knit-fabric grille elevates the overall aesthetic. This is more apparent on the white colorway than the black, and luckily the lighter color is exactly what was sent to me for review. Bose also opted for a glass top where the competition typically uses a plastic panel or just buttons. The glass portion doesn't extend all the way to the edges though, so there's room for the up-firing drivers to do their thing.
Another excellent design choice was the volume controls. Bose installed a touch-enabled, circular panel that allows you to spin your finger clockwise and counterclockwise to raise and lower the volume. You can also just tap the "+" or "-" if you'd rather. There's an area in the middle of the circle that you can tap to play, pause or skip tracks, as well as touch-based controls for Bluetooth, disabling the soundbar's microphone and summoning Alexa. All of that is positioned on the right side of the glass panel.
Inside, Bose arranged a collection of nine drivers for the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar's acoustic architecture. There are six full-range drivers, two of which are up-firing and the other four are front facing. Additionally, a center-mounted tweeter assists with dialogue clarity, while two so-called PhaseGuide drivers spread sound horizontally. To calibrate all of that for your living room, Bose's CustomTune feature uses the microphone in your Android or iOS device to analyze the space (speaker layout, surfaces and seating) and optimize the soundbar's output.
Like most soundbars these days, the Lifestyle Ultra only has a single HDMI eARC input. This isn't a problem per se, but if you need HDMI 2.0 passthrough for things like game consoles, just note that it's not available here.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is very much a plug-and-play device. Once you connect it to power and your TV, it's ready to go. However, you'll want to download the Bose app and run the CustomTune audio calibration ASAP to tailor the soundbar's output to the acoustics of your living room or home theater space. Of course, if you add either the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer or Lifestyle Ultra Speakers to the soundbar, you'll need to repeat the CustomTune process.
Once all of that is complete, the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar provides a solid boost to your TV audio. The up-firing and PhaseGuide drivers offer a pleasant level of immersion and dimensional audio, which is apparent on shows like Drive to Survive and Masters of the Air. The bass output is the most impressive thing about this soundbar, though. It's enough that users in small to medium spaces likely won't immediately feel the need to add a subwoofer. Even after several weeks of testing, I'm still baffled by the low-end performance when a sound effect demands that portion of the frequency range.
This bass is abundantly apparent for music, too. Sylvan Esso's "Flood Season" has ample lows for the bass guitar riffs and kick drum, while more bass-heavy tracks, like Russian Circles' "Empath," maintain the tonal depth without getting muddy. I also appreciate how the center tweeter allows vocals to consistently float on top of the mix. This makes albums like Hayley Williams' Ego Death At A Bachelorette Party particularly enjoyable.
As I already mentioned, Bose allows you to expand your home theater system with the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer and Lifestyle Ultra Speakers. Unless you have a larger space, or just crave the extra immersion that rear speakers can provide when watching movies or TV shows, I don't think either are absolutely necessary here.
The speakers are $349 each and the sub comes in at $899, but if you opt for the Home Theater Set or Surround Sound Set (Lifestyle Ultra bundles), you can save a few hundred dollars. (Oddly, Bose doesn't offer savings on the Extra Bass Set, which is the soundbar and subwoofer).
I tested the add-ons one at a time. First, I added the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer to the soundbar — perhaps the most likely additional purchase for most people. This achieves the obvious result of adding more bass, which could be preferential if you plan for the Lifestyle Ultra gear to pull double duty as your main music setup. But even in my living room, which is open to the main dining area and kitchen, the soundbar alone was still adequate for music.
I then added two Lifestyle Ultra Speakers as rear units, which I quickly discovered would be my preferred way to bolster the soundbar's performance. Since the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar holds its own in the bass department, its only true deficiency is directional audio and overall immersion. Add those two speakers to the rear and that weakness is fixed, and disabling the subwoofer doesn't result in much sacrifice to overall output. I only really noticed a big difference in certain scenes with really booming effects, like certain parts of the first episode of Masters of the Air (no spoilers from me) .
AirPlay, Google Cast and Spotify Connect are all available on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar for quick and easy music streaming. You can also opt for Bluetooth, if you prefer, but I find the three methods I mentioned are more convenient for getting audio from a phone or laptop to a soundbar.
The Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar does well enough on its own that Bose's primary competition is other companies that claim they've built all-in-one TV speakers that don't need a separate subwoofer. My top pick in that category is Samsung's QS90H , which costs $99 less at full price. This 7.1.2-channel soundbar not only provides adequate bass without a sub, but it has Samsung's Convertible Fit tech that allows you to place it flat or mounted upright. Sensors in the soundbar then reconfigure the output based on how it's sitting. Samsung included lots of other features, but some of them, like Q-Symphony, require a recent Samsung TV to use.
Another excellent option for a true all-in-one soundbar is the Sonos Arc Ultra . The company's flagship model is equipped with Sound Motion technology that handles the bass in a 9.1.4-channel setup. That last number indicates two additional height channels compared to the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar and the QS90H. The Arc Ultra not only has more channels overall, but it also contains more drivers than either the Bose or Samsung options, with 14 of those total. At full price, the Arc Ultra costs the same as the Lifestyle Ultra, but Sonos currently has it on sale for $899 .
Editor's note: Bose is offering a $200 discount on the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar through October 11.
Perhaps Bose's hesitance to label the Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar as an all-in-one unit comes down to sales. I'm sure the company would prefer for you to buy the pricey subwoofer for a speaker combo that's common to living rooms. I'd recommend spending extra money on a pair of Lifestyle Ultra Speakers instead, and configure your home theater for better immersion rather than overly booming bass.

articles.title_orig: From H-1B to CEO: How Satya Nadella traveled the path the U.S. just cut off for Microsoft workers
articles.title_zh: From H-1B to CEO: How Satya Nadella traveled the path the U.S. just cut off for Microsoft workers
articles.content_orig:
India called comments by U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance about immigrants from the country "deeply offensive" in an official government statement published on Friday.
Vance said on Thursday that the Trump administration wants foreign and local companies to "employ American workers," and that they "cannot lay off American workers and then replace them with foreign indentured servants."
He was speaking as the U.S. Department of Labor announced it would suspend Microsoft , Adobe and several major Indian information technology companies from its Permanent Labor Certification program, meaning they cannot apply for permanent residency for their employees on H-1 B visas.
Around 70% of H-1B beneficiaries in 2025 were born in India , per official data .
In a statement on Friday, India's Ministry of External Affairs accused Vance of using " terminology that carries painful historical and colonial legacy connotations."
"Such descriptions are unwarranted and ignore the fact that Indian professionals in the United States are highly educated and skilled contributors to its economy and innovation ecosystem," the statement said.
Vance's office did not immediately respond to a comment request from CNBC.
Vance was critical of Microsoft, accusing the company of replacing 6,000 laid-off workers with people on H-1B visas.
The Indian foreign ministry assured its citizens that measures announced by the U.S. will not affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents.
"Talent mobility adds value to both economies," the statement said, adding that the suspensions "do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries."
The Indian companies affected by the ban include Cognizant , Infosys , Capgemini, Tata Consultancy Services , Wipro and HCL .
NASSCOM, the IT industry body, said in a statement that Indian technology companies have "significantly reduced their dependence on H-1B visas" over the last few years, and are expanding domestic hiring to their U.S. workforces.
The largest Indian IT company, Tata Consultancy Services, said its H-1B applications were in "single digits" in the last two years, and it intends to hire another 15,000 people in the U.S. over the next five years.
In June, a federal judge blocked the $100,000 H-1B visa fee U.S. President Donald Trump imposed last year.

articles.title_orig: Trump to push US officials to use Defense Production Act to raise oil, fuel output, three sources say
articles.title_zh: Trump to push US officials to use Defense Production Act to raise oil, fuel output, three sources say
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Jarrett Renshaw and Nicole Jao
WASHINGTON/NEW YORK, Oct 9 (Reuters) - US diesel prices remain at near-record highs, up 70% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began despite two recent moves by President Donald Trump to boost supplies: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and ‌expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing the average ‌US diesel price to $6.28 a gallon on Friday, according to motorist group AAA.
"Aside from a recession that hammers consumption, the only thing that can prevent oil prices from rising further and ​put them on a sharp downward trajectory is a durable end to conflicts in the Arabian Gulf and between Russia and Ukraine," said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan Energy Group. "Otherwise, policy options range from marginal to counterproductive."
High fuel prices have made it harder for Trump and his Republican Party to defend narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections. The cost of living is the top item cited by voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll, and high diesel prices put particular ‌pressure on traditional Republican constituencies: farmers, truckers and rural ⁠voters.
Trump's approval rating is at a career-low 32%, according to the poll.
The administration has touted a G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of oil and petroleum products as a major step to help ease prices, but those barrels ⁠appear to largely cover what remains of a March emergency release by International Energy Agency members, rather than new supply.
A White House official disputed that characterization, saying the earlier commitments were not specifically for refined products. The administration negotiated for the previously committed barrels to be front-loaded with diesel and released on a tight timeline beginning ​immediately, ​the official said.
The White House said Trump was focused on easing temporary disruptions while pursuing ​longer-term energy policies.
The administration's other major initiative, an executive ‌order allowing red-dyed diesel on public roads through year-end, has drawn limited industry uptake. The fuel is chemically identical to what trucks normally burn but is tinted to show it is exempt from the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal highway tax.
The order defers the federal tax and waives penalties for burning off-road fuel on highways. But major retailers and marketers remain wary of selling it because of unclear tax liabilities, logistical hurdles and the risk of fines when trucks cross state lines.
The tax savings are relatively small with diesel prices above $6 a gallon.
David Fialkov, who lobbies on behalf of NATSO, a trade group for truck stops ‌and travel centers, said the White House appeared to be encouraging the supply chain to ​sell dyed fuel through channels not traditionally used for highway diesel, but said that most ​reputable retailers and marketers were unlikely to do so.
John Tirado, president ​of New Jersey-based commercial fuel supplier Summa Energy, called the red-dyed diesel plan "a Band-Aid on a much bigger problem."
The White ‌House said more than 4,000 retailers distribute dyed diesel. It ​said Treasury Department guidance will clarify the ​rules, allowing drivers to use it without federal tax or penalty. It said the savings should outweigh any detour costs for truckers seeking the fuel.
"The fundamental problem facing the US is not taxation but an exceptionally tight global market for refined products," said Caspian Conran, lead economist ​at Baringa, citing disruptions to energy flows from the ‌Middle East and reduced refining output elsewhere.
He described the measures as short-term steps ahead of the election that could provide "probably a few ​weeks of relief," rather than a durable solution.
(Reporting By Jarrett Renshaw in Washington, Additional reporting by Nicole Jao in New York ​and Timothy Gardner in Washington; Editing by Nathan Crooks, David Gregorio, Rod Nickel)

A leaked deposition shows Senate candidate Ken Paxton defended himself against fraud allegations by claiming he doesnât remember and blaming his now-estranged wife.
The Texas attorney generalâs never-before-seen 2014 testimony from a fraud probe was given to The New York Times by someone who opposes his election and was then independently verified by The Times.
It was the latest leak to hit the struggling MAGA candidate in the must-win race, as he has also faced a slow drip of audio leaks.
The deposition was part of a U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) investigation into a technology start-up in McKinney, Texas, called Servergy Inc.
Senate candidate Ken Paxton, pictured campaigning with President Trump on October 7, has been hit with another leak, this time a 2014 deposition in a fraud probe.
The SEC grilled Paxton, who represented the state district where it was based, on whether he hid that the company compensated him for recruiting investors, the Times reported, as its founder, Bill Mapp, was accused of making false statements to investors.
Paxton has long fought allegations of corruption and questions about his ballooning wealth for years while serving in public office, but he has never been convicted.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
Speaking under oath to federal lawyers in 2014, Paxton defended himself while using phrases such as âI donât rememberâ and âI donât recallâ more than 200 times, according to the report.
He passed the buck to his now-estranged wife, Angela Paxton, when asked about his tax returns, which appeared to contradict part of his testimony.
âI havenât prepared a tax return in a long time because I donât have time, so typically, actually my wife actually does them,â Paxton said.
Ken and Angela Paxton in 2021. She filed for divorce last year.
Lawyers questioned Paxton about emails in which the start-upâs founder, Mapp, appeared to offer him a commission for recruiting investors.
Paxton claimed he did not remember reading many of Mappâs emails, according to the report, and did not perform services for the company.
When confronted with his own tax returns, showing Paxton had disclosed $100,000 for âlegal servicesâ to the company, he pointed the finger at his then-wife.
Paxton met with Mapp at a Dairy Queen to give him a check for his investment with Servergy, but Mapp rejected the money and instead gifted him 100,000 shares of stock, the report said.
âHe said, I canât take your money. God doesnât want me to take your money,ââ Paxton told lawyers in the deposition.
When asked why Mapp would give him shares for free, Paxton said in the deposition, âIt was not logical,â and claimed, âBill is a spiritual person.â He also said he did not ask a lawyer if it were appropriate to accept the shares.
He also told the lawyers he could not remember where the certificate proving he owned the stocks was.
Paxton listed the shares as stocks on his annual financial reports filed with state ethics regulators, but a Texas ethics law expert told The Times that Paxton may have violated state rules by not disclosing the shares as a gift.
During the deposition, Paxton also said he had more than $400,000 invested in various companies, but he said he did not have time to track his investments.
The federal judge dismissed the SECâs fraud case against Paxton in 2017, saying he had no obligation to tell investors he had received something of value from the company.
Last year, Angela Paxton filed for divorce, accusing her husband of infidelity. The Daily Beast asked her for comment on the report but did not immediately hear back. She declined to comment to The Times.
The Daily Beast also asked for comment from Paxtonâs campaign. In response to The Times, a Paxton adviser called the leaked deposition a distraction and argued the candidate âhas been politically persecuted for years for standing up to the establishment, and Texans have seen through it every time.â

articles.title_orig: Intel Is Reportedly Launching New CPUs On Old Sockets That Support DDR4 Memory
articles.title_zh: Intel Is Reportedly Launching New CPUs On Old Sockets That Support DDR4 Memory
articles.content_orig:
This is, of course, due to the AI-fueled RAMpocalypse.
We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
Intel is reportedly releasing new CPUs built on LGA 1700 sockets, according to motherboard manufacturer Gigabyte . The LGA 1700 has been around since 2021, which is a really long time in processor land. Why use relatively ancient technology in brand-new processors that are set to release next year? It all comes down to the price of memory, according to a report by PC Gamer .
LGA 1700 sockets offer support for both DDR5 and DDR4 memory, so the running theory is that upcoming refreshes of Raptor Lake and Alder Lake processors will be configurable to use DDR4 RAM. This is likely to accommodate the ongoing AI-fueled RAMpocalypse , in which memory prices have skyrocketed. Simply put, DDR4 RAM is a lot cheaper than DDR5. Folks can pick up a 32GB DDR4 kit for around $210 , but a 32GB DDR5 kit costs upwards of $480 .
Intel hasn't confirmed this theory, but VP Robert Hallock recently said that Raptor Lake chips would be sticking around for "years to come." He also suggested that DDR4 integration is one of the primary reasons. "LGA 1700 is still a good socket. Lots of people are still interested in DDR4, so we'll keep offering," he said.
This isn't that surprising, given that many of the company's current line of processors can already be configured to use DDR4 memory. DDR4 isn't as fast as DDR5, but the older memory type is still fine for the vast majority of modern PC games . Testing has revealed that DDR5 sticks deliver a 1 to ten percent FPS improvement. However, this largely depends on the resolution the player chooses and the GPU.

articles.title_orig: Home on verge of collapse as high tide hits Long Beach Peninsula
articles.title_zh: Home on verge of collapse as high tide hits Long Beach Peninsula
articles.content_orig:
Learn more about what storm season means for Long Beach and how you can be prepared at LBPost.com/elnino . Support useful, community-centered reporting like this with a donation .
City inspectors have declared several buildings on the Peninsula unsafe to enter after Hurricane Rachel’s high surf and tides chewed away at the shoreline, tearing apart a section of a wooden wall that is the neighborhood’s last line of defense against the ocean.
Officials issued a notice Thursday night that a large section of the bulkhead, left exposed after waves from Hurricane Marie ripped away its surrounding sand , was badly damaged over the past day and left a gap that allowed water to reach homes and side streets.
Residents stood in shin-deep flooding on Friday, with vehicle access closed at 62nd Place. Waves continued to chew at homes’ foundations along the shoreline and tear planks from the boardwalk. At least one home in the 6500 block of Seaside Walk appeared close to collapse.
Laath Martin, a city spokesperson, said inspectors are still assessing the extent of the bulkhead and boardwalk damage.
Crews rushed to make emergency repairs, pump water off the streets and fill in the exposed section with roughly 1,000 sandbags. The city is bracing for rain this weekend, and more high tides and surf are expected.
Read more: Why one small stretch of Long Beach keeps getting pounded with damaging waves
Inspectors surveyed homes threatened by water damage and red-tagged two buildings containing three units in the 6400 and 6500 blocks of Seaside Walk. The red tag means they’re too dangerous to enter.
Craig Nakano, a spokesperson for the city’s Community Development Department, said Friday that nobody has been displaced by the tagging. One property was under construction, he said, while the other was confirmed by the owner to be vacant.
A third building received a yellow tag, which means its owner may go in briefly to collect belongings but may not stay. Nakano confirmed that the owner had already found somewhere else to stay.
Two buildings were already yellow-tagged after damage from Hurricane Marie weeks ago. The latest damage brings the total to five damaged Peninsula structures, two red-tagged and three yellow-tagged. The tags are preliminary, and a red tag can be downgraded to yellow once repairs are made and inspectors sign off. Inspectors will keep checking homes twice a day.
The latest bout of strong waves — whipped up by Hurricane Rachel — came just weeks after other hurricane-charged swells battered the Long Beach coast and the Peninsula .
The city is planning a multimillion-dollar dredging project to rebuild the stretch of Peninsula beach that’s been eroded. Long-term fixes are expected to be even more expensive.
In the meantime, storms keep rolling in.
Bryan Lewis, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said high surf and tide are expected to rise precipitously each day through Sunday, with tides reaching 7.5 feet high on Saturday and nearly 8 feet high on Sunday morning around 10 a.m. Waves are currently ranging from 4 to 7  feet high, but are expected to rise to up to 8 feet by Sunday, he said.
Conditions on Sunday evening and Monday morning, he said, will mirror Saturday, and likely will not relent in strength until Wednesday morning.
The NWS expects to announce a flood warning later Friday. They currently have an advisory running through Tuesday. Warnings are usually triggered when coastal buoys the Service monitors — in this case ones in the San Pedro Channel and city harbor — are routinely hit with high enough surf, Lewis explained.
This storm could also bring rain and wind. The city expects up to a half-inch of precipitation this weekend and gusts strong enough to knock down trees and power lines.
“Protecting our residents is our top priority as high surf and erosion impact our Peninsula community,” Mayor Rex Richardson said in a statement. He praised emergency crews and urged residents to “be prepared and follow City guidance.”
Lewis said rain showers could start in the area as early as Friday night and Saturday morning, with a second storm system hitting the area on Monday. Showers are expected to total between a half inch and three quarters of an inch of rain.
“This will bring additional rain, so that’s kind of separate from what tropical storm Rachel could be responsible for,” Lewis said.

articles.title_orig: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.title_zh: Trump establishes committee to investigate Federal Reserve's Lisa Cook in latest effort to fire her
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Trump eases Russia sanctions to allow Putin to release diesel fuel onto the global market amid price spike
President Donald Trump on Friday signed an order directing the attorney general and other top federal officials to establish a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, in his latest attempt to fire her.
“By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, I hereby establish a committee of inquiry (Committee) to investigate allegations that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook made false statements in connection with one or more mortgage instruments,” read a presidential memorandum posted to the White House website.
It said that the committee would “investigate the allegations against Governor Cook and report to me whether there is ‘cause’ for Governor Cook’s removal.”
“Governor Cook may submit a written position statement to the Committee regarding the allegations,” the memorandum said.
The unprecedented White House announcement comes after a top White House official in August wrote a letter to Cook , saying that Trump was considering removing her from the Federal Reserve board.
The White House memorandum said that Cook “shall appear at the hearing and be examined by the Committee,” as well as “present argument, written evidence, and written witness statements regarding the evidence and allegations.”
The committee is set to meet Nov. 5 for the hearing, two days after the midterm elections. No president has ever fired a top Fed official.
“In light of the President’s repeated statements that he has already decided to fire Governor Cook — regardless of the facts and evidence —  we have grave doubts that this ‘hearing’ is a legitimate one that would conform to the law,” said Abbe Lowell and Norm Eisen, Cook’s attorneys.
“But if it is anything close to objective, the conclusion will be that Governor Cook did not commit mortgage fraud, leaving no cause to remove her from the Federal Reserve Board.”
Lowell and Eisen said they have engaged with the White House to determine if this is a “genuine” process and that Cook “welcomes the opportunity to present the facts so she can clear her name and demonstrate there is no legal basis to fire her.”
The memo follows a Supreme Court ruling in June, which allowed Cook to remain in her job for now. But the justices did not permanently block Trump from removing Cook, instead ruling that she had the right to an opportunity to defend herself.
Trump’s latest move stems from allegations first leveled against Cook in August 2025 by Federal Housing Finance Agency chief Bill Pulte. Trump amplified those allegations on social media and, citing a “criminal referral” he said Pulte had sent to the Justice Department, attempted to remove her from the Fed’s board.
Pulte alleged that Cook committed mortgage fraud, however documents obtained and reviewed by NBC News later revealed that Cook declared that the property in question was to be used as a “vacation home” and not her primary residence.
The Federal Reserve declined to comment on Friday’s developments.
Other top Trump administration officials, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, reportedly have similar mortgage situations.
Former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Environmental Protection Agency Administrator Lee Zeldin have all called more than one property their “primary residence” on mortgage applications, according to a report last year from ProPublica .
Cook, a governor on the Federal Reserve’s board, has a permanent vote on interest rates. Trump and Pulte’s attacks on Cook came amid a long-running pressure campaign by the administration to get the U.S. central bank to cut interest rates.
“President Trump is convening an illegitimate show trial in his dangerous quest to illegally take over our nation’s central bank,” said Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, which oversees the Fed.
“Instead of playing judge in a kangaroo court of his own making, Trump should end the war in Iran and cancel his chaotic tariffs,” Warren said.
Trump also recently resumed his attacks on another Fed governor, Jerome Powell. Trump claimed Sept. 30 that the former chairman was complicit in cost overruns for a construction project at the central bank’s headquarters. However, an inspector general’s report found no wrongdoing.
Trump responded to the report by writing on social media, “He should be forced to resign, IMMEDIATELY! If he doesn’t resign, he should be sued, at the highest level, by the United States Government, for either corruption or incompetence.”
Following the post, Attorney General Todd Blanche told Bloomberg News , “We’re not reopening a criminal investigation into him.”
Powell has remained on the Fed’s board despite the end of his term as chair, breaking with tradition. As long as Powell remains on the board, the Trump administration is denied the opportunity to name a new board member of the president’s choice.
Cook has consistently maintained that she did nothing wrong.
Just weeks ago, Cook’s lawyer told the White House for a second time that, “There is no legal basis for President Trump to remove Governor Cook for cause.”
“An inadvertent error is not fraud, as the President and a third of his cabinet should know because they reportedly did the same thing,” Abbe Lowell said Aug. 26. “These attacks on Governor Cook are not about real estate paperwork; they are an attempt by President Trump to force the Federal Reserve to bend to his will.”
Lowell said he and Cook were prepared to continue to fight “any illegal attempt to remove Governor Cook.”
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.

articles.title_orig: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.title_zh: Ex-German Chancellor Schröder attends Putin's birthday bash
articles.content_orig:
Former German Chancellor Gerhard Schröder attended Russian President Vladimir Putin 's birthday party, the Kremlin said Thursday.
Putin celebrated his 74th birthday in Moscow on Wednesday. The Kremlin said Putin learned that Schröder was on a business trip in the Russian capital via Russian media reports.
"The president invited his old friend to his home," the Kremlin said, with the Russian government releasing pictures of Schröder and Putin smiling and clasping hands.
Schröder , who is 82 years old, was in Moscow visiting one of the branches of the new Hyperglobus supermarket chain. The ex-German chancellor was named to the chain's supervisory board last week.
Hyperglobus was originally part of German retail company Globus Holding, which operates the Globus supermarkets in Germany and the Czech Republic.
Globus Holding also had supermarkets in Russia, but divested its stake last year, with those stores thus being spun off into separate company Hyperglobus.
Schröder, a member of the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) , served as Germany's chancellor from 1998 to 2005.
Since leaving the chancellery, Schröder has worked for Russian state-owned energy firms and has also maintained personal contact with Putin.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Schröder's fondness for Russia has drawn controversy, particularly since the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Schröder's tax-payer financed Berlin office was closed in 2022 over his involvement in the Russian energy sector, and he has also faced calls by fellow party members to be expelled from the SPD.
Schröder, however, has survived the attempt to be kicked out of his party.

articles.title_orig: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.title_zh: US diesel prices remain high despite Trump's moves to boost supplies
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
By Jarrett Renshaw and Nicole Jao
WASHINGTON/NEW YORK, Oct 9 (Reuters) - US diesel prices remain at near-record highs, up 70% since the US-Israeli war on Iran began despite two recent moves by President Donald Trump to boost supplies: pressuring allies to release emergency reserves and ‌expanding access to tax-exempt red-dyed diesel.
The wars in Iran and Ukraine have triggered a severe global fuel supply crunch, pushing the average ‌US diesel price to $6.28 a gallon on Friday, according to motorist group AAA.
"Aside from a recession that hammers consumption, the only thing that can prevent oil prices from rising further and ​put them on a sharp downward trajectory is a durable end to conflicts in the Arabian Gulf and between Russia and Ukraine," said Bob McNally, president of Rapidan Energy Group. "Otherwise, policy options range from marginal to counterproductive."
High fuel prices have made it harder for Trump and his Republican Party to defend narrow congressional majorities in the November 3 midterm elections. The cost of living is the top item cited by voters in a Reuters/Ipsos poll, and high diesel prices put particular ‌pressure on traditional Republican constituencies: farmers, truckers and rural ⁠voters.
Trump's approval rating is at a career-low 32%, according to the poll.
The administration has touted a G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of oil and petroleum products as a major step to help ease prices, but those barrels ⁠appear to largely cover what remains of a March emergency release by International Energy Agency members, rather than new supply.
A White House official disputed that characterization, saying the earlier commitments were not specifically for refined products. The administration negotiated for the previously committed barrels to be front-loaded with diesel and released on a tight timeline beginning ​immediately, ​the official said.
The White House said Trump was focused on easing temporary disruptions while pursuing ​longer-term energy policies.
The administration's other major initiative, an executive ‌order allowing red-dyed diesel on public roads through year-end, has drawn limited industry uptake. The fuel is chemically identical to what trucks normally burn but is tinted to show it is exempt from the 24.4-cent-per-gallon federal highway tax.
The order defers the federal tax and waives penalties for burning off-road fuel on highways. But major retailers and marketers remain wary of selling it because of unclear tax liabilities, logistical hurdles and the risk of fines when trucks cross state lines.
The tax savings are relatively small with diesel prices above $6 a gallon.
David Fialkov, who lobbies on behalf of NATSO, a trade group for truck stops ‌and travel centers, said the White House appeared to be encouraging the supply chain to ​sell dyed fuel through channels not traditionally used for highway diesel, but said that most ​reputable retailers and marketers were unlikely to do so.
John Tirado, president ​of New Jersey-based commercial fuel supplier Summa Energy, called the red-dyed diesel plan "a Band-Aid on a much bigger problem."
The White ‌House said more than 4,000 retailers distribute dyed diesel. It ​said Treasury Department guidance will clarify the ​rules, allowing drivers to use it without federal tax or penalty. It said the savings should outweigh any detour costs for truckers seeking the fuel.
"The fundamental problem facing the US is not taxation but an exceptionally tight global market for refined products," said Caspian Conran, lead economist ​at Baringa, citing disruptions to energy flows from the ‌Middle East and reduced refining output elsewhere.
He described the measures as short-term steps ahead of the election that could provide "probably a few ​weeks of relief," rather than a durable solution.
(Reporting By Jarrett Renshaw in Washington, Additional reporting by Nicole Jao in New York ​and Timothy Gardner in Washington; Editing by Nathan Crooks, David Gregorio, Rod Nickel)

Moderna ( MRNA ) stock popped 9% on Friday after the New York Times reported new details about an effort to accelerate cancer vaccine development. Investors saw the mRNA biotech company, in particular, as a beneficiary.
Other pharmaceutical stocks, including Pfizer ( PFE ), BioNTech ( BNTX ), and Merck ( MRK ), also rose.
According to the New York Times, the new initiative is a public-private partnership — similar to the effort that produced COVID-19 vaccines — that involves the National Institutes of Health (NIH), the NIH's nonprofit arm, researchers, pharmaceutical and biotech companies, advocacy groups, other nonprofits, and patients.
Stacey Adam, a senior clinical officer at the NIH's foundation, told the New York Times that she expects the program to launch in December. In 2024, the UK launched a similar program, called the Cancer Vaccine Launch Pad .
Moderna is viewed as a leader in mRNA cancer treatments. The stock soared in August on positive results for a melanoma treatment , developed with Merck.
Year to date, Moderna stock is up 627%.

articles.title_orig: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.title_zh: Get in the Spotlight With the Line Life Podcast
articles.content_orig:
A few years ago, I partnered with Danielle Blanchette and our team from T&D World to launch the  Line Life Podcast. Our mission was simple: to bring the stories from the pages of T&D World magazine to the airwaves.
Due to the nature of their jobs, lineworkers are not in an office working behind a computer day in and day out. Instead, they are slipping on their work boots, packing their tool bags and heading out in the field to keep the power flowing to the customers in their service territories.
Because lineworkers spend a lot of time traveling from one location to the next in their bucket trucks, we wanted to give them a way to listen to our field-focused Electric Utility Operations (EUO) stories on the go.
We started with only audio stories, and then we started branching out into interview-style episodes. For the last few years, I've recorded interviews with lineworkers and their loved ones for future episodes of the Line Life Podcast.
With the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo Week only a few days away, we're excited to offer that opportunity again to the Lineman's Rodeo attendees. Swing by the T&D World Booth #001 (in the breezeway between the ballroom and the exhibit hall) to sit down with me, Amy Fischbach, for a conversation about your career in the line trade.
I air interview-style episodes on the first and third Fridays of each month and audio stories on the second and fourth Fridays on Podbean and in your favorite podcasting app.
To see all the episodes we've recorded over the years, go to linelife.podbean.com . You can also check out our new International Lineman's Rodeo Roundup page on our T&D World website to see the past Rodeo-related episodes.
I look forward to seeing you during the 2026 International Lineman's Rodeo and putting you in the spotlight for the Line Life Podcast!
Amy Fischbach is the Head of Content for T&D World magazine and manages the Electric Utility Operations section. She is the host of the Line Life Podcast , which celebrates the grit, courage and inspirational teamwork of the line trade.  She also works on the annual Lineworker Supplement and the Vegetation Management Supplement as well as the Lineman Life and Lineman's Rodeo News enewsletters. Amy also covers events such as the Trees & Utilities conference and the International Lineman's Rodeo. She is the past president of the ASBPE Educational Foundation and ASBPE and earned her bachelor's and master's degrees in journalism from Kansas State University. She can be reached at [email protected] .
